message:
openPMD: Fix Reader of Scalar Records

For scalar openPMD `records` such as a temperature field,
a particle charge attribute, etc. the `record` itself is identical
to its `record component`.

This commit fixes the detection of `record` attributes specific
to fields (meshes) by checking either on the `record component`
(scalar records) and if the attribute is not found there at the
`parent` group (for vector records) level.

author: Alexander Blinne <alexander.blinne@uni-jena.de>
message:
Enhancements for map_coordinates method

**Incompatible adjustments to last version**
* `postpic.Field` method transform is renamed to `map_coordinates`, matching the underlying scipy-function.
* `postpic.Field.map_coordinates` applies now the Jacobian determinant of the transformation, in order to preserve the definite integral.

In your code you will need to turn calls to `Field.transform` into calls to `Field.map_coordinates` and set the keyword argument `preserve_integral=False` to get the old behaviour.

**Other imrpovements and new features**
* `postpic.Field` has a new method `map_axis_grid` for transforming the coordinates only along one axis which is simpler than `map_coordinates`, but also takes care of the Jacobian
* `postpic.Field.topolar` has new defaults for extent and shape
* `postpic.Field.integrate` now uses the simpson method by default

"pre-commit" is a wrapper arount "run-test" such, that it can be
symlinked to serve as a git pre-commit hook. Doing so will ensure to run
all tests before commiting. The wrapper also stashes changes that will not
be commited and restores them afterwards.

message:
Merge pull request #156 from Ablinne/reimplemented_vtk

Reimplemented the vtk export and added methods to unstagger fields:

* `postpic` has a new function `unstagger_fields` that will take a set of staggered fields and returns the fields after removing the stagger
* `postpic.Field` has a new method `adjust_stagger_to` to adjust the grid origin to match the grid origin of another field
* `postpic` has a new function `export_vector_vtk` that takes up to three fields and exports them as a vector field in the `.vtk` format
* `postpic` has a new function `export_scalars_vtk` that takes up to four fields and exports them as multiple scalar fields on the same grid in the `.vtk` format

author: Stephan Kuschel <stephan.kuschel@gmail.com>
message:
change to a expression based interface for particle properties

The new particle interface is expression based and its performance is automatically increased by the numexpr package.

Per partice properties are must now be accessed via the __call__ method of the MultiSpecies object. The expression given can be anything that evaluates on a per particle basis including to an array of boolean values which speeds up particle sorting drastically. The MultiSpecies.filter has been added for convenience. For valid examples see examples/simpleexample.py.

The namespace is separated and recognizes all symbols which can be accessed by postpic.particle_scalars. If the symbol used is not found the module scipy.constants will be searched. See the doctring of postpic.MultiSpecies.__call__.

The old interface to access particle properties by functions is still working, however DeprecationWarnings will be issued and it is to be removed in the future.

message:
Merge pull request #172 from Ablinne/ab/image-import

Field: added method to load image files

Changed the io methods to have the following meaning:

* `postpic.Field` has methods `.loadfrom` and `.saveto`. These can be used to save a Field to a ` .npz` file for later use. Use `.loadfrom` to load a Field object from such a file. All attributes of the Field are restored.
* `postpic.Field` has methods `.export` and `.import`. These are used to export fields to and import fields from foreign file formats such as `.csv`, `.vtk`, `.png`, `.tif`, `.jpg`. It is not guaranteed to get all attributes back after `.export`ing and than `.import`ing a Field. Some formats are not available for both methods.

message:
Merge pull request #184 from Ablinne/ab/axis_spline_interpolation

Axis: use spline interpolation for fallback grid/grid_node

This changes the defaults for `Axis.grid` and `Axis.grid_node`. Before, the defaults were created using linear interpolation of whatever was explicitly given. Now, spline interpolation is used. This should make grid/grid_node more "compatible" with each other in case of non-linear grids. In the case of linear grids, nothing is changed, except for roundoff errors (this is reflected in the tweaks for some of the test cases).

message:
Merge pull request #74 from Ablinne/albn/enhancement-kspace

Albn/enhancement kspace

* change `Field.shift_grid_by` to be able to choose between fourier and linear interpolation
* add `helper.omega_yee_factory` to get omega(k) function for yee solver
* add `helper.kspace to calculate` the k-space from E and B fields of a single dump
* add `helper.kspace_epoch_like` to calculate k-space from E and B fields while using the linear interpolation, that epoch uses. This reduces ghost peaks from 10^-1 to 10^-2 in field, which is an improvement from 10^-2 to 10^-4 in spectrum for a frequency close to Nyquist frequency (5 grid points per wavelength). Results will be much better for better sampling.

message:
less memory consumption of _SingleSpeciesAnalyzer internals.

The _SingleSpeciesAnalyzer is now requesting the data on demand of the
application. This is particularly useful if working with a huge number
of particles and only requesting some of their properties. This leads to
significantly less memory consumption. See benchmark results below.

Additionally data will be cached inside the _SingleSpeciesAnalyzer if
and only if the 'compress' function was used. Since sorting of particles
by conditions takes time (particles.py: line 60), this leads to a speed
up of the data processing (compared to no caching).

Benchmark with 72e6 particles creating 4 figures making heavy use of
compression functions.
Measured with '/usr/bin/time -v':
                      wall time , max resident set size
before this commit:      11.7sec, 6.78GB
no caching:              17.9sec, 2.44GB
only compressed caching: 11.3sec, 2.74GB  <= selected now.
always caching:          10.9sec, 3.40GB

message:
Merge pull request #165 from skuschel/ku/dev

Various small fixes, improvements and documentation updates

* `postpic.MultiSpecies.createField` has now keyword arguments (`bins`, `shape`), which replace the corresponding entries from the `optargsh` dictionary. The use of the`optargsh` keyword argument has been deprecated.

* Overload of the `~` (invert) operator on `postpic.MultiSpecies`. If `ms` is a MultiSpecies object with filtered particles (created by the use of `compress` or `filter`), then `~ms` inverts the selection of particles.

* The dumpreader now checks if the dumpidentifier point to the same file.
This avoids wrong "False" results as the same file can be represented by
different path strings.

* fig bug when multiple particle filters were used
A shallow copy of the singlespecies object needs its own copy of the
_compressboollist. Otherwise a second call of compress on this object
will also alter the original.
This has now been fixed.

message:
solution with testOutliers within plotResiduals

testOutliers doesn't work if simulationOutput is not a DHARMa object (it needs the information if integerResponse is TRUE or FALSE. However, plotResiduals allows for vectors in the simulationOutput (ensureDHARMa will create a DHARMA object but without "integerResponse" information). So, first, I test if the. simulationOutput is a vector, and a warning if so. Then I proceed with plotting (or not) the outliers and coloring dots according to the outlier test.

message:
scan query: use columns instead of dimensions (#148)

Scan queries use the columns parameter (string array) to define the
dimension to return [1]. Currently, pydruid is incorrectly filling a
dimensions parameter, which ends up being ignored (and the scan query
always return all dimensions).

[1] http://druid.io/docs/latest/querying/scan-query.html

Signed-off-by: Alejandro del Castillo <alejandro.delcastillo@ni.com>

message:
scan query: use columns instead of dimensions

Scan queries use the columns parameter (string array) to define the
dimension to return [1]. Currently, pydruid is incorrectly filling a
dimensions parameter, which ends up being ignored (and the scan query
always return all dimensions).

author: Magnus Henoch <magnus@gameanalytics.com>
message:
Don't throw away error messages from Druid

In certain cases, Druid will return an error message in JSON format in
the body of the HTTP response.  However, PyDruid would attempt to
parse the HTTP reason phrase as JSON instead, which wouldn't succeed
as it is something like "Bad Request" and "Server Error".  Fix this by
parsing the response body instead.

Also do the same thing for error code 400 ("bad request"), not just
500.  For "bad request" errors, there is usually a clue as to what's
wrong with the query in the error message, so it's worth displaying
the error message instead of discarding it.

Testing the new powertrain system based on the ChShaft 1D objects.
Currently it has:
- thermal engine with torque curve
- torque converter

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Add quadratic inertial terms in IGA (gyroscopic and centrifugal effect). The gyro effect could be neglected in many cases where the beam has slow rotations, but the centrifugal term was really needed for the case of beams with center of mass being offset from centerline, as when using ChInertiaCosseratInertiaAdvanced.
Note that for the moment those quadratic terms are added to the internal forces, hence they contribute to the K and R stiffness and damping tangent matrices, in detail the gyroscopical effect might change the K matrix adding some unsymmetry - this is the reason why in rotordynamics the K and R change as speed ramps up evein in linearized models, where the eigenvalues split in forward whirl/backward whirl modes in the Campbell diagrams that consider gyroscopical effects.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor visualization with meshes for vehicle wheel rims:

- a rim mesh is assumed to be provided (in a Wavefront OBJ file) with respect to a frame with origin at the tire center and Y axis pointing towards the *outside*
- the mesh is translated and rotated as needed, based on the wheel offset (for the case of double-wheel axles) and the vehicle side on which the wheel is mounted
- this eliminates the need to define two separate wheel classes (e.g. HMMWV_WheelLeft and HMMWV_WheelRight); similarly, it eliminates the need for two separate wheel JSON specification files
- the name for the visualization asset is automatically set to be the stem of the input filename

The code is less cluttered by obsolete functions.

message:
GPU solver uses a lot less memory now, I moved the preprocessing stage to the iteration kernel by creating a new device function. Even though data is re-computer many times, it actually runs faster because there are fewer global memory accesses, (less data is saved and read from global). 
Because the data is not preprocessed, the memory used to store the data is not necessary, this saves a of GPU memory. Theoretically with a C1060 (4GB) it should be possible to run a simulation with 4 million particles and 22 million maximum contacts. I'm going to test this soon.

author: Ruochun Zhang <rzhang294@euler.wacc.wisc.edu>
message:
Fix the inconsistency among multiple runs with the same input, when using MULTISTEP friction model and no mesh

- The inconsistency is caused by the non-associative property of float additions. 2 blocks can collaborate in contact detection, so even though the same set of events is detected every time, the order they appear in big array can be different. When the forcs are added with different orders the outcomes can vary.
- The system is highly chaotic, small differences lead to large discrepancy in the end.
- We just sort the set of events before adding the force, problem solved.
- FRICTIONLESS model and mesh interaction is not touched in this commit. They can be fixed, but will require the same data structure and workflow as MULTISTEP, likely to remove their performance advantage. A decision is needed.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
IMPORTANT change in the way that ChSystem does the management of its lists of bodies, links etc. Internally, there are three lists/vectors, that is: one for ChBody items, one for ChLink items, one for all other ChPhysicsItem that are not bodies or links.
Previously, if using the mysystem.Add( myitem) command, the Add() machinery detected in which of these three lists the item had to be put, but it did not take into consideration that someone might have inserted a ChBody-inherited item, so that was add anyway to the list of 'other ChPhysicsItem' stuff.
Indeed, now it works in the following more reasonable way: if one adds a ChBody-inherited item, such as ChBodyEasySphere or such, it will be sent to the list of ChBody.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor ChTire reporting of tire forces.

Use two separate functions:
- GetTireForce() returns the generalized tire force (point of application, force, moment) to be passed to the vehicle system and applied to the wheel body.   For tire models that use underlying Chrono functionality (e..g, contact for ChRigidTire or constraints for ChDeformableTire), this function *must* return zero force and moment (else tire forces are double counted).
- ReportTireForce() returns the generalized tire force, for reporting purposes or for obtaining the tire force in a co-simulation framework.  It is passed a pointer to the terrain system (for tire models where that is irrelevant, pass 'nullptr').

ChRigidTire is currently the only tire model which reports tire forces from interaction with an SCM terrain.

TODO: report tire forces from the interaction of a deformable tire and SCM terrain.

NEW feature. This new  ChBeamSectionProperty  machinery is used for the ChElementBeamIGA  element only, but in future it may supersede the ChBeamSection. The idea is that a ChBeamSectionProperty contains an elasticity model, and a plasticity model. For the moment, a simple lumped plasticity model (axial direction only for the moment) is available, but in future other might come. This architecture will be used also for continuum (materials for tetrahedrons etc.) so that plasticity can be used.
Plasticity can have isotropic and kinematic hardening.
Also, the elasticity model can support basic symmetric sections (ChElasticityTimoshenkoSimple) or sections with arbitrary offset, rotation, and shear center (ChElasticityTimoshenkoAdvanced).

Major changes in the ChPovRay  exporter for POVray.
- Previously, it was not able to generate an usable project (directory with .ini, .pov, .asset etc) other than in the current directory of the .exe, doing otherwise generate a project with broken links between the files. - There is no need to put the name of optional "anim" and "output" sub-directories in the SetPictureFilebase() and SetOutputFilebase() functions like we did SetPictureFilebase("anim/pics"), now these functions take just the name of the files like SetPictureFilebase("pics") and the name of the subdirectory is initialized by default to be "anim" and "output". author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Add global free functions for dealing with the Chrono data.

While this set of changes do not address the issue of where the data/ directory lives, they offer the following:
(1) it isolates the hard-coded default location (namely "../data"), relative to the location of the executable programs, to a single place (in ChGlobal.cpp)
(2) it allows external projects that depend on Chrono to access the default Chrono data files without having to copy the data/ directory.  Instead, simply invoke SetChronoDataPath() to specify where the Chrono data directory is (for example, in the Chrono source tree or the Chrono install tree)

The three new functions are as follows:
(1) SetChronoDataPath(): specifies the location of the Chrono data/ directory. The default is "../data/".  Note that this function is not thread-safe.
(2) GetChronoDataPath(): retrieves the location of the Chrono data/ directory (thread-safe)
(3) GetChronoDataFile(): obtains the complete filename given the name of a file or subdirectory relative to the location of the Chrono data directory (thread-safe)

This method, which must be overriden by derived classes, creates and returns a pointer to a new body. Note that the body is not attached to the system.

This change facilitates writing generic utility functions that create bodies.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add simple models of hydraulic circuit components and hydraulic actuators.

These are based on the lumped fluid theory.
Models for a hydraulic cylinder, a directional valve, and a throttle valve are currently implemented.
Two models of hydraulic actuators, one using two volumes and the other three volumes, are provided.

The hydraulic actuator models are implemented as physcis items with external dynamics and are modeled with ODEs describing the time evolution of the valve input and of the various pressures in the circuit.

The hydraulic actuators can be used stand-alone, for example in a co-simulation setup (in which case they receive the current actuator length and rate of change and return a force) or else can be attached between to Chrono bodies.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Report tire forces differently for the case of co-simulated tires.

Tires that have actual physical models (such as rigid tires or FEA-based tires) must report zero force and moment (because the tire forces on the associated wheel body are applied implicitly, either as contact forces or as link reaction forces).  However, when the tire is co-simulated, GetTireForce() must return the actual force to be applied to the associated wheel body.

Other tire models (namely those modeled as force elements, such as Pacejka, Fiala, Lugre) ignore this flag and always calculate and report the actual tire force to be applied to the wheel body.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New way to compute the rotational lumped inertia for IGA beams. The previous version had few shortcomings:
- the Ixx polar inertia was computed based on a "rectangle" model where sides of the rectangles were the size of the visualization shape (that might be unset /unrelated in some cases, and it was a temporary hack anyway)
- the Izz and Iyy thin section per-unit-length inertia values were simply not used, it just used the near-zero value suggested by some textbooks, not a bit issue for thin beams, but could have been underestimated for very thick beams.
Needs to be benchmarked to see the benefits.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
The previous bool() operator for ChSharedPtr and ChSmartPtr were potentially dangerous because the compiler could implicitly cast bool to integer etc.
To avoid this potential risk of misunderstanding, now I implemented it by using the 'safe bool idiom', as used in boost shared pointers, so the bool implicit cast can be used only for  tests like
  if (mysharedptr) ...
Note that this is also possible with more typing..
  if (!mysharedptr.IsNull())
Note also that, when we'll migrate to C++11 / C++0x , there will be no need of this odd 'safe bool idiom', because we could use the 'explicit' in
  explicit operator bool() ..

author: Mike Taylor <mtaylor22@wisc.edu>
message:
Updating the new ANCF elements so that the fast ANCF specific generalized force due to gravity method is now efficiently calculated at every internal force call.

This change accounts for cases where the acceleration due to gravity for the containing system changes between time steps (for each during a unit test with a gravity load).
Prior to this, it was assumed that the acceleration due to gravity for the containing system was constant and it was set prior to the precalculation phase for the elements.

message:
Improvement on TimoshenkoFPM and IGA (#331)

Several improvement on Timoshenko with fully-populated matrix(FPM) and IGA from last pull request:

This is helpful for me in my personal project, to allow me to fall back and do the dynamics iteration again with a more rigorous solver settings. A better solution is to develop this functionality inside ChTimestepperHHT because I think in this way the overall speed is fastest.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Hack in Bullet to avoid troubles with triangle meshes vs Bullet convexes.
The fact is that Bullet uses 'contact persistence' to build a minimal set of multiple contact between 2 shapes, even if its colision algo (ex GJK) produces a single contact per step. Then the manifold of contact is just 'updated' from time to time, and contacts that were created previously will be deleted only when they became separated by a certain amount. The problem is that with meshes of FEA triangles, this does not work, since 1) triangles might deform b) the bullet algo for manifold removal is based on shape translation/rotation, but triangles in triangle meshes do not have an affine roto/translation.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Add option to disable keyboard inputs and/or use data from file.

The Irrlicht GUI driver can be in one of three input modes:
- KEY:  driver inputs are obtained from the keyboard (A, D for steering, W, S for throttle/brake and Z, X, C for gears)
- FILE: driver inputs are played back from a data file (suing an embedded ChDataDriver object)
- LOCK: driver inputs are kept fixed at their last values

To switch between these modes, use K (keyboard), J (lock), and L(data file).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Address issues related to memory alignment and Eigen matrices.

(1) For classes which have members of fixed-size Eigen types, ensure that heap allocation uses the correct operator new (which allocates properly aligned memory).  This is done by adding the macro EIGEN_MAKE_ALIGNED_OPERATOR_NEW  in the public part of the class.

(2) Since std::make_shared may use placement new and not operator new, provide a chrono-specific replacement for make_shared which guarantees use of operator new.   This requires replacing all uses of std::make_shared<> with chrono::make_shared<> when wrapping pointers to classes with fixed-size Eigen members.

(3) Note that creating shared pointers for types other than those above can still use std::make_shared.  However, for uniformity and to reduce confusion/errors, we may want to use chrono::make_shared throughout.

Clamp regions for ray-casting to available grid index range.

Note:
For a flat SCM terrain patch, this clamping is only needed if using a visualization mesh (as we would access mesh vertices out of bounds).
The rest of the grid-based SCM algorithm accommodates an infinite grid.
For an SCM terrain patch initialized from a height-filed map, this clamping is also needed in order not to access the heights table out of bounds (this could be relaxed by defining the undeformed terrain height beyond the specified limits to be that at the slosest map boundary).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor collsion system (WIP):

- eliminate dependency of ChSystem and contactables (ChBody, ChContactSurface, etc) on a particular collsion system implementation.
- eliminate automatic construction of a collision system within a ChSystem. Instead, a concrete collision system is constructed in user code and associated with the Chrono system.
- parsing and processing of all collision shapes in all collision models of all contactable objects occurs during initialization of a collision system.
- update all classes derived from ChBody.
- update FEA contact surfaces (nodes and mesh).
- update all utility and convenience classes and functions for creating physics items..
- modify ChCollisionModel to be non-virtual.  A ChCollisionModel holds a pointer to an implementation-specific object which can be used by a concrete implementation of a collision detection system.  This member variable is used to defer run-time operations to the actual collision system implementatino (e.g., collision shape position updates, calculation of current axis-aligned bounding box, etc).
- update the Bullet collision system to new design.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor Chrono::Distributed.

- Add support for gathering contact forces acting on a body or on a user-specified list of bodies
- Add support for overriding position of a body (or list of bodies), properly accounting for change in ownership
- Add custom collision callback to model a collection of collision planes for defining computational domain boundaries
- Add option for run-time visualization of simulation on master rank with Chrono::OpenGL
- Add support for integration in external co-simulation framework
- Fix ChSystemDistributed::AddBody which can be used to add a body to the system without user intervention.  This function performs its own location checks and adds the body only to the appropriate ranks.  It also increments the global number of bodies.   While potentially slower for systems with large number of bodies, this function allows using various Chrono utilities such as those for generating granular material with an API consistent with Chrono and Chrono::Parallel
- Fix ChSystemDistributed::AddBodyAllRanks to automatically increment the global body counter
- Add function to mark and check the 'master' process in the ChSystemDistributed intra-communicator. For efficiency, certain functions report information only on this single rank. This saves a potentially unnecessary scatter operation (if needed, such an operation should be performed in user code). By default this is rank 0 in the system's intra-communicator.
- Fix bugs in body data exchange to ensure proper ownership hand-over (include missing quantities: material properties, collision families, etc.)
- Clean up

  I opted for the current solution (i.e. adding an additional argument) because:

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Automatically set path to Chrono data directory for Python demos.

- this must be an absolute path or a path relative to the location of the python demos
- controlled by the CMake variable PYCHRONO_DATA_PATH
- default value is appropriate for the case where the user builds Chrono::Python from sources
- appropriate values for this path (os-specific) are set in the scripts used to generate the conda packages

- the CMake variable PYCHRONO_DATA_PATH is used to generate and install an __init__.py which calls SetChronoDataPath with the specified path
- as such, if executed from their default locations, python demos need not explicitly call chrono.SetChronoDataPath
- python vehicle demos still need to set the path to Chrono::Vehicle data directory, typically `veh.SetDataPath(chrono.GetChronoDataPath() + 'vehicle/')`

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Replace "speed tolerance" with "force tolerance".

- iterative solvers use a stopping criteria based on the norm of the residual. For the speed solver, this is a check at impulse level.
- in principle, this tolerance should be tightened if/when the step size is decreased.
- instead of prescribing the tolerance for a residual at impulse level, we now require the user to prescribe a tolerance at force level (independent of step size).
- internally, the tolerance actually used by the speed solver is obtained by multiplying the user-specified tol_force by the current time step size.
- the default value for tol_force is set at 1e-3

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
The .i files of the Python wrapper (unit_PYTHON) and the .h files must stay in sync.
Yesterday a commit broke the unit_PYTHON because the SWIG wrapper got a mismatch between ChQuaternion.h and ChQuaternion.i (those .i files are used to tell to SWIG what must be wrapped into a Python class/function). By the way, these .i files are most often simple .h references because SWIG can just parse the corresponding .h file and decide by himself, but for ChVector.h and ChQuaternion.h and few other classes, this was not possible so I had to override the funciton definitions line by line.
Therefore, when one changes something in the .h file for ChVector and ChQuaternion etc., he must also check to update the corresponding .i file if this is necessary.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add a generic FSI interface, agnostic of the particular fluid solver type.

This generic FSI interface intermediates the data exchange betwen the associated Chrono multibody system and fluid solver using Chrono data types (i.e., independent of the fluid solver).
A particular fluid solver may be paired with a custom FSI interface (as is the case with the current SPH-based fluid solver).
The custom FSI interface is potentially more performant than the generic one, as it can work directly with the fluid solver memory and thus save an additional data copy that is inherent in the generic FSI interface.

message:
Having moved the static std::string irrlicht_default_obj_dir into the ChIrrAppInterface caused the SWIG python wrapper generator to fail.
Tho fix this, I moved back such static  irrlicht_default_obj_dir  in the original place (the ChBodySceneNodeTools.h), that was never processed by SWIG and so the SWIG error is gone.
Note, by the way, that such static variable was  used only by functions in ChBodySceneNodeTools, plus in the ChIrrAppInterface to define the directory for fonts.
Since the use of static vars is not a good practice (exp. here in a .h, that might result in multiple static data per each .cpp object), for defining font directory we now introduced a SetFonts() function in ChIrrAppInterface, and the ChBodySceneNodeTools is kept here in its original form only for backward compatibility (but will removed in future, anyway, because  now we have the ChAsset - based visualization system)

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Shared pointers that were passed by reference, now are passed by value.
It worked only for single classes, but if using complex class inheritance, this is needed because if one passes a ChSharedPtr<DERIVED> where a ChSharedPtr<BASE> is expected then a static cast would be needed, with static_cast_chshared<>(), and it would require tto much typing.
Of course passing the shared ptr by value means also a copy, but the overhead should be almost negligible (this issue with shared pointers by value or by reference has been recently discussed by H- Sutter et al., and looks like there is no need to pass by reference hoping for better performance...)

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add support for location-dependent coefficient of friction for interactions of rigid bodies with RigidTerrain.

- In this case, the interaction is resolved using the underlying Chrono frictional contact mechanism and therefore requires a traversal of all current contacts and appropriate modification of the composite material.
- In the context of vehicle simulations, this feature is needed for vehicles with rigid tires and for tracked vehicles driving over a RigidTerrain for which a user-defined ChTerrain::FrictionFunctor was provided.
- Since this involves relatively expensive calculations at each time step, use of this feature is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by calling RigidTerrain::UseLocationDependentFriction.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Optimization. The DEM method does not require that contacts are created before the distance is smaller than an 'outward' safety envelope, as it is needed in DVI.
Instead, in classical DEM, contacts have an effect only when there is some interpenetration.
So, here in ChSystemDEM I set the default outward envelope to 0, instead than default 0.03 that was in the normal ChSystem.
This means that also bounding boxes will be more 'tight', less potential contacts are created, the collision detection stage is faster, less RAM is used (especially for small granular particles whose size was comparable to that 0.03 envelope!)

As such, all unnecessary checks were removed.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor and extend templates for continuous-band track vehicles.

- two different templates are provided, different in how the track web is modeled
- BAND_BUSHING represents a web model based on rigid segments connected with bushing elements
- BAND_ANCF represents an FEA web model based on ANCF shell elements
- a common sprocket type (ChSprocketBand) interacts with either type of continuous-band track
- the track-sprocket collision relies on a custom collision (for collisions between the sprocket and the track shoe's tread body) and the underlying Chrono collision system (for collisions between the sprocket and the track web)

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Support for adding and updating ChShaft elements.

- These are 1-dof elements that have associated (scalar) inertia and only allow rotation about their axis.

- Due to limitations imposed by the base ChSystem class, shaft elements must be added as "other physics items" (else their variables would not be properly accounted for in ChSystem::Setup).  Currently, we maintain pointers to such elements in a separate list, ChSystemParallel::shaftlist (this means we duplicate data already present in the list ChSystem::otherphysicslist)

- We use a private member function, AddShaft, which eventually should become an override of a virtual function ChSystem::AddShaft.  This function is private so that a user is forced to use AddOtherPhysicsItem to add a shaft to the system (see above)

- For now, all parallelization of the loops over shaft elements is disabled.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: New ChFunctionRotation_SQUAD, a further type of rotation function generator. This uses the SQUAD algorithm as in Shoemake 1987 paper. It interpolates between quaternions as in cubic Bezier curves. In my implementation, a sequence of interpolated quaternions is expected, and the in-between Bezier control points ("handles") are generated automatically. Different from the ChFunctionRotation_spline, that implements N order quaternion splines where quaternions pass 'near' the control points, this method exactly passes through the control points.

For a ChBody, this function performs all operations that were explicitly performed in the chrono_parallel code.  However, for a ChBodyAuxRef this function is overriden: it first calls the base class (ChBody) update then performs the required update for the noncentroidal reference frame.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Enable full RPATH linking for installed executables

By default, CMake links executables with full RPATH only in the build tree and
clears the RPATH before installing targets.  This means that, by default, installed
executables will not find the shared libraries (unless these are installed in a default
location, such as /usr/local/lib).

With this change (lifted directly from the CMake wiki), executables are relinked with
the install RPATH.  This allows running the installed executables regardless of the
installation location and without having to change LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Change specification of solver tolerances, consistent with recent Chrono changes.

Changes:
- iterative solvers use a stopping criteria based on the norm of the residual. For the speed solver, this is a check at impulse level.
- in principle, this tolerance should be tightened if/when the step size is decreased.
- instead of prescribing the tolerance for a residual at impulse level, we now require the user to prescribe a tolerance at force level (independent of step size).
- internally, the tolerance actually used by the speed solver is obtained by multiplying the user-specified tolerance value by the current time step size.

TODO:
- some solvers (e.g. BiCG) use additional stopping criteria which should be based on different tolerance values (currently, we use the same tolerance as for the stopping criteria based on the residual norm)
- some solvers (e.g. MINRES) use a combination of relative and absolute tolerance. The absolute tolerance is the tolerance above.  The relative tolerance should be a separate user-specified value.  For now, the relative tolerance is hardcoded to be 0.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
HHT: switch to relative + absolute NR convergence test (in ACCELERATION mode).

NR is declared converged if either the L2 norm of the residual is below the absolute tolerance or the WRMS norm of the update is less than 1.
The WRMS norm test is a relative + absolute tolerance test:
    ||v||_WRMS = sqrt{ sum{(v_i * w_i}^2 / N }
where the weights are calculated as
    w_i = 1 / (reltol * |v0_i| + abstol)
with v0 the current solution (i.e., the solution at previous step).
WRMS norms for the update in the accelerations and Lagrange multipliers are calculated separately and use possibly different absolute tolerances.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New operators for doing transformations with mixed types ChFrame / ChFrameMoving. This was not possible explicitly in previous API and forced to promote a ChFrame to a ChFrameMoving by constructing it before doing the * or >> operation with a ChFrameMoving.
This is implemented now for both  * operator (right to left coord. transformation) and >> operator (left to right transformation).
Note that when doing  ChFrame * ChFrameMoving one could have the option of implementing either ChFrame  or ChFrameMoving as return type. I decided to return the type 'at the end' of the kinematic transformation, that is the right most in the * expressions and the leftmost in the >> expressions, so I decided that  ChFrame * ChFrameMoving  returns a ChFrameMoving , whereas  ChFrameMoving *  ChFrame  returns a ChFrame.  In most cases this fits the needs of the programmer and does not introduce too overhead as returning always the more complex type ChFrameMoving.
In future I'll add also mixed operators for ChCoordsys vs ChFrame  and ChFrameMoving.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Improvement of  structural damping. The previous implementation of internal forces affected also the matrices used for geometric stiffness, so the convergence of implicit solvers was affected in a bad way. Now the internal damping forces are computed separately, but I avoided building the stiffness matrix K for computing F=-alpha*K*v otherwise it takes more CPU effort than needed, I rather use the factorized version of K (and this also opens the way, in future, to provide custom damping constitutive laws).
Now the Reissner element works well also with HHT and I can consider it to be reliable and usable in production.
Future changes might be related to speed optimizations.

author: Andrew Seidl <dev@aas.io>
message:
cmake: enable ccache if available

No special configuration necessary, simply install `ccache`. CMake will
automatically enable if found and if using a supported generator
(Makefiles and Ninja).

Cache may be cleared via `ccache -C`

On my laptop, complete build with a clean build dir:

- empty cache: 74.6s
- warm cache: 5.3s

Obviously will not see that dramatic of speed up during everyday
development, but most builds should be noticeably faster.

(For comparison, running `cmake` with no options takes 5.4s.)

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Fix for GCC: use the keyword 'template' for disambiguation.

Relevant paragraph in the C++11 standard:
When the name of a member template specialization appears after . or -> in a postfix-expression or after a nested-name-specifier in a qualified-id, and the object expression of the postfix-expression is type-dependent or the nested-name-specifier in the qualified-id refers to a dependent type, but the name is not a member of the current instantiation (14.6.2.1), the member template name must be prefixed by the keyword template. Otherwise the name is assumed to name a non-template.

message:
Add eff_radius member to ChCollisionInfo and ChContactTuple.

- this value is relevant only for SCM
- this represents the effective radius of curvature at a contact point, obtained as 1/r_eff = 1/rA + 1/rB
- if a collision system does not / cannot calculate this for a particular pair, a default value is used
- the default effective radius value can be changed through the (static) function ChCollisionInfo::SetDefaultEffectiveCurvatureRadius
- modified the functor class ReportContactCallback to include eff_radius as argument to OnReportContact
- updated Chrono::Parallel to allow setting the (global) value of edge_radius (fictitious radius of curvature for collisions with a corner or an edge)

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Add core utility classes to implement Bezier 3D curves.

The class ChBezierCurve encapsulates a piecewise cubic Bezier approximation to a 3D curve, specified as a set of knots and two sets of control points (vertices of the control polygons)
- if the control points are not provided, they are calculated so that the resulting Bezier curve is a spline interpolant of the knot points
- the class provides functions to evaluate the curve as well as first two derivatives for a specified interval and a given curve parameter

The associated class ChBezierCurveTracker provides a robust mechanism for tracking the closest point on a Bezier curve to a given location
- it provides a mechanism for resetting the tracker
- it uses time coherence to provide good initial guesses for the underlying Newton iteration

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add ChSolver pure virtual method SolverRequiresMatrix() to indicate whether or not the Solve phase requires and up-to-date problem matrix.

- This flag is needed when the solver is used within a modified Newton iteration where it is used to decide whether or not the problem matrix must be evaluated even though a call to Setup will not be made.
- Typically, direct solvers only need the matrix for the Setup() phase. However, iterative solvers likely require the matrix to perform the necessary matrix-vector operations.
- As such, direct solver will usually return 'false', while iterative solver will return 'true'.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Improve implementation of chrono::make_shared.

- Recall that `std::make_shared` does not work properly for classes that use aligned memory allocation (because they have fixed-sized Eigen matrices as members).
- Such classes override `operator new` with a custom Eigen implementation.  However, `std::make_shared` uses `placement new` and therefore does not use the custom operator new.
- For these cases, the solution is to explictly construct the shared_ptr.
- This is done with two specializations of a function `chrono::make_shared` which check whether or not the wrapped object provides a custom `operator new`.  If it does not, `chrono::make_shared` simply defaults to using `std::make_shared`.
- All Chrono code, demos, and tests, as well as user code should therefore only use `chrono::make_shared`.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Major trouble with Python unit is fixed.
The problem is that, with the recent C::E source, the class hierarchy has been heavily changed, and the .i files in the unit_PYTHON did not reflect the actual hierarchy.
But the big trouble is that the new class hierarchy of C::E has some multiple inheritances in classes, and this caused the python wrapper to fail.
Basically, the default behaviour of pointer casting of function args in SWIG did a void* reinterpret_cast that previously was working (luckily) but now this is not possible anymore because a following reinterpret_cast to custom classes might cause a 'slicing' in the class offsets (vtables of classes with multiple inheritance is not guaranteed to be aligned to offset 0 !)
So the workaround is to adopt custom typemaps where the shared pointers get converted in SWIG_ConvertPtr using an intermediate ChSharedPtr<> of the proper base class, then it is passed to the function wrapper, then it is deleted.
Last but least, the %DefChSharedPtr() macro can be called in a smarter way.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Fixes to ChSolverMKL and use of Eigen sparse matrices:

- combine analyzePattern() and factorize() into a single call to compute() made in ChSolverMKL::Setup
- when providing space estimates for the sparse system matrix, use reserve() with vector argument (to preallocate memory for nonzeros in each row)
- implement function setZeroValues (in plugin extension header) to reset all nonzeros to a value of 0 (without any other effects on sizes or allocated memory)
- in ChgSystemDescriptor::ConvertToMatrixForm, use conservativeReset (to ensure no memory deallocation when matrix sizes do not change) and call setZeroValues (to prepare matrix for injection by physics items)
- replace user-provided estimate for number of nonzeros with user-provided estimate of matrix sparsity, defined as 1 - nnz/(n*n).

message:
New ChColorAsset . If one object of this class is added to the asets of a body, all assets should get the specified color (it is up to the converters, ex for OpenGL or POV or Irlicht, to handle this behavior.)
If the ChColorAset is enclosed in a ChAssetLevel, only the shapes included in that level should get the color. This is similar to the behavior of ChTexture, btw., and it is very memory efficient.
Previously, one had to use a ChVisualization asset, but the name was misleading, and the confusing fact is that ChVisualization was also a base class of other shapes like spheres etc.
Some bugs in postprocesser and Irrlicht converter have been fixed too.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: Simplify the mesh generated by ChVisualShapeFEA in case of FEA triangle shell elements (ex. the BST shells). Previously it created TWO times the needed triangles, each triangle being in original and normal-flipped direction (that was because the Irrlicht visualization system cannot visualize both sides of a mesh with both correct lighting, unless making inward and outward triagles), and this wasted memory and create issues in other rendering heads (ex Blender with path tracing) cause overlapped triangles give floating point jitter banded artifacts. So just generate one triangle with one sided normal, and let the rendering head handle it.

author: Hammad Mazhar <hammad.maz@gmail.com>
message:
GPU solver uses a lot less memory now, I moved the preprocessing stage to the iteration kernel by creating a new device function. Even though data is re-computer many times, it actually runs faster because there are fewer global memory accesses, (less data is saved and read from global). 
Because the data is not preprocessed, the memory used to store the data is not necessary, this saves a of GPU memory. Theoretically with a C1060 (4GB) it should be possible to run a simulation with 4 million particles and 22 million maximum contacts. I'm going to test this soon.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add workaround for Chrono::Gpu limitation related to size of computational domain.

- Chrono::Gpu assumes that the domain is centered at the origin *and* large enough to accomodate any collision objects that may be added later on (such as the wheel here)
- When using HCP sampling, the granular terrain height changes very little during settling and, if defining the domain to be the initial volume in which particles are initialized, the wheel ends up being  created outside the domain.
- For now, enlarge the computational domain by 1 (we cannot properly do this as we do not know anything about the wheel at this point) and ensure the granular material is created starting from the bottom boundary of the domain.

message:
New "thermal engine" class, defining a torque curve and a throttle modulation. The computed torque is applied to shaft 1, say the crankshaft, and the negative torque is applied to shaft 2, say the motor block, that gets the reaction.
Note that the throttle model is simplified, it simply scales the value of the torque curve linearly, as Tfinal = T(w)*throttle
In future we may add a 2D map as Tfinal=T(w,throttle).

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Disable update of visualization assets where appropriate.

During the step integration, the Update() function is called twice, once at the current state and again after the state was advanced to the new time.
During the former, there is no need to update visualization assets.
For models with complicated assets, this can significantly reduce the cost of an integration step (up to 2x)

message:
The node element ChNodeFEAxyzD with [position,direction]  dofs for the 'cable' beam (see the ChElementBeamANCF) now uses a more proper LCP variable type, that is the new ChLcpVariablesGenericDiagonalMass class. That class can represent nodes with N dofs which have a diagonal mass associated. To this end one previously could have used the ChLcpVariablesGeneric class, that implied the use of n x n block matrix, but that was overkill.
Note that by default the lumped mass is set to zero in the node, in most cases the mass will be added by the finite element and no 'atomic' mass is needed.

message:
New classes that define various models for generating the damping matrix R^ of the reduced subassembly. To be used when doing myassembly->SwitchModalReductionON()
At the moment I created:
ChModalDampingNone()                    // no damping (also default)
ChModalDampingReductionR(*my_assembly)  // transforms the original damping matrix of the full subassembly
ChModalDampingReductionR(full_R_ext)    // transforms an externally-provided damping matrix of the full subassembly
ChModalDampingCustom(reduced_R_ext)     // uses an externally-provided damping matrix of the reduced subassembly
ChModalDampingRayleigh(0.01, 0.05)      // generates a damping matrix from reduced M ad K using Rayleygh alpha-beta
ChModalDampingFactorRmm(zetas)          // generates a damping matrix from damping factors zetas of dynamic modes
ChModalDampingFactorRayleigh(zetas,a,b) // generates a damping matrix from damping factors of dynamic modes and rayleigh a,b for boundary nodes
ChModalDampingFactorAssembly(zetas)     // generates a damping matrix from damping factors of the modes of the subassembly, including masses of boundary

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add a second type of drawbar pull rig, ChVehicleCosimImposedAngVel.

This mechanism enforces a prescribed wheel angular velocity.
A linearly increasing resistive force is applied against the forward motion of the vehicle and the experiment is ended when the vehicle stops.
At each time, the vehicle forward speed and resulting slip are calculated and stored together with the current resistive force (DBP).
This experiment produces the entire slip-DBP curve at once.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Adding handy constants to represent very common 90 degrees rotations via quaternions. In the past this always meant long syntax like
    chrono::Q_from_AngAxis(chrono::CH_C_PI_2, chrono::VECT_X)     or such. Now this can be shorter -and also more intuitive- by doing:
    chrono::Q_ROTATE_Y_TO_X
There are six constants for all 90° rotations. Note that for -90° one can do the conjugate as !Q_ROTATE_Y_TO_X or just do  Q_ROTATE_X_TO_Y.
For the 180° rotations (flips) there are three constants Q_FLIP_AROUND_X, Q_FLIP_AROUND_Y, Q_FLIP_AROUND_Z.

By default, self-collision are allowed and included in collision detection.

If a family is provided, all collision models contained in the contact surface are assigned to that family and collisions are disabled within the family.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor Chrono::Vehicle tire models:

(1) consistent reporting of tire kinematics is provided through accessor functions of the base class ChTire (e.g., GetSlipAngle, GetLongitudinalSlip, etc.)
- these quantities are computed in a consistent manner for all tire models (within ChTire::CalculateKinematics) and the accessor functions cannot be overriden by derived classes.
- these quantities are reported relative to the ISO vehicle reference frame.
- a particular tire model is allowed to use different definitions in their internal calculations and report these internal quantities through additional accessor functions (e.g., GetSlipAngle_internal, GetLongitudinalSlip_internal, etc)

(2) allow user to specify the method used for terrain-tire collision detection
- options include: single point of contact below disc center, 4 contact points below disc center, envelope-based calculation
- the collision method is specified through an optional argument to the tire Synchronize method (with the default being "single point of contact")
- this functionality is available for all Chrono::Vehicle tire models (except RigidTire which uses the underlying Chrono collision detection mechanism)

(3) extend all Chrono::Vehicle tire models to properly account for possible location-dependent terrain coefficient of friction
- all tire models query the terrain system to find the terrain coefficient of friction 'mu' at the current tire (x,y) location
- the resulting tire forces and moments are scaled by a factor mu/mu0, where 'mu0' is a reference coefficient of friction (corresponding to the given tire parameters, typically representing a dry paved road)

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: Fix issue in PSOR with the new POU splitting of masses and forces. In detail, POU mass splitting not needed because PSOR iteration needs M^-1 blocks to be considered in 'clipped' format, not in 'additive' format. Luckily enough M blocks are on the diagonal and no M from elements is supported, so we can use the same property used in the lumped diagonal solver: y_clipped = f_mpimerge (A_clipped * x_additive).  Whereas in general what is used would be y_clipped = f_mpimerge (A_additive * x_clipped)

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: BUG FIX. This was a nasty bug that happened only in a special situation, using ChLinkMotorRotationSpeed or a ChLinkMotorLinearSpeed with some time stepper settings and with FEA. The fact is that those links also contain a ChVariable. In this case, IntLoadResidual_CqL()  was polluting the vector with wrong values because offsets were wrong. Offsets used by IntLoadResidual_CqL() are those'offset' that are stored in ChVariables, which in this case were not matching with the 'offset_w' that are stored in ChPhysicsObject. This because the former are counted and set by the ChSystemDescriptor at each variable injection, the latter are set by ChAssembly at each Setup(). In general those processes give the same offsets (which also poses a question: there is a redundancy of offset management, no need for the one in the descriptor, the one in Setup() would suffice, in future the ChSystemDescriptor should get the variables injected with the offsets already set by the owning ChPhysicsObject). But the old version of Setup() made the bookkeeping for 1)bodies, 2)links, 3)FEA etc. All other bookkeepings are 1-3-2 instead, including variable injection. So the mismatch with the offsets in the ChSystemDescriptor in speial circustamces. Fixed by swapping the order to 1-3-2 also in Setup().

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Introduce sprocket templates:

- A sprocket template defines a gear profile and provides the custom collision callback to process contacts between the sprocket gear and track shoes in the containing track assembly.
- A given sprocket template (in particular, a given gear profile) must be consistent with the type of track shoe (e.g. ChArcSprocket and ChSinglePinShoe).
- A concrete sprocket class provides parameterization of the gear profile;  a concrete track shoe class provides parameterization of the contact shape for interaction with the sprocket.

Note: this obsoletes the utility free functions in ChSprocketProfiles.{h,cpp}

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
IMPORTANT. Change in API of shared pointers. Previous code will work as before, but in some cases you will need to add  "DynamicCastTo<...>()" when casting shared pointers.
Background---
Previously, casting between ChSharedPtr shared pointers was too 'liberal', in the sense that it also allowed casting bwtween unrelated pointer types.
Not only this was inconsistent with the way that C++handles normal pointers, but also this left room to programmer mistakes.
Solution---
In the new ChSharedPtr it happens that:
- casting between shared pointers is automatic if upcasting from a specialized class to a parent class, or between same classes, as in c++ pointers; in this case your code does not need any changes.
- casting between shared pointers in downcasting from a base class to a specialized class now explicitly REQUIRES A DYNAMIC CASTING, otherwise you get a compiler error.
- casting between unrelated pointers will generate a compiler error at compile time.
The dynamic casting can be obtained by using the new   DynamicCastTo<>()  function, or by using the new    dynamic_casting_chshared<>(...)   method that is very similar to c++ dynamic_casting.
This means that in this commit we had to change many parts of the code where a base shared pointer was previously cast to specialized classes by doing simply
   ChSharedPtr<MySpecialClass>myspecialized = mybase;
into the new:
   ChSharedPtr<MySpecialClass>myspecialized = mybase.DynamicCastTo<MySpecialClass>();
Note that this requires more typing, but it is less prone to misunderstandings than the previous approach.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Add utility Chrono::Vehicle classes to implement a steering PID controller.

The core functionality is implemented in the abstract base class ChSteeringController
- implements basic functionality to control the error between the location of a sentinel point (a point at a look-ahead distance in front of the vehicle) and the current target point.
- a derived class must implement the CalcCurrentTarget method
- error derivative is estimated using backward finite differences
- error integral is estimated using the trapezoidal integration scheme, with a step-size

The class ChPathSteeringController is a derived class which sets the target location as the closest point on a Bezier path to the sentinel point.
- it uses a Bezier path tracker object to robustly calculate the target location

Additional derived classes could set the target location from other sources (e.g. by interfacing with a camera sensor model).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add ChSystem boolean flags is_initialized and is_updated.

- This comit implements only the logic for changing their value on system modifications.
- is_initialized: if false, it indicates that an initial setup is required.
- is_initialized is set to false on system construction and set to true upon a call to ChSystem::SetupInitial. Addition of a physics item sets it back to false (currently only for ChMesh, as other physics items do not require an initial setup)
- is_updated: if flase, it indicates that a new system update is required
- is_updated is set to false on system construction and set to true at the end of a successful integration step.  Modifications to the system topology (addition/removal of physics items) sets it back to false.  Also, an NSC system is declared "out of date" (is_updated = false) if there are contacts, as these introduce unilateral constraints.

One can add items to it using AddBoundary() or AddInternal(), where the latter generate a mechanism that will be substituted with mode synthesis after a modal analysis, whereas the items added via AddBoundary will persist even when in modal assembly mode  and can be used to attach the modal assembly to other mechanisms using constraints etc.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Large number of changes in most classes, to use a new class factory mechanism.
- A new class factory has been designed; it used an unordered map instead of a linked list. More modern design, etc.
- Instead of using ChClassRegister<myclass> a_registration_object;   now use the CH_FACTORY_REGISTER macro.
- Instead of using the CH_RTTI macro, use the CH_FACTORY_TAG macro in the .h headers, in class definitions. There is no need to specify the class parent or root, like before. This makes the code less cluttered and there are no issues when there are multiple inheritances.
- The old RTTI emulation is obsoleted, now the serialization just uses the CH_FACTORY_TAG and CH_FACTORY_REGISTER stuff.
- Do not use  CH_FACTORY_REGISTER  for abstract classes (classes that have at least one pure virtual function, interfaces etc.), compiler will give error.
- Do not use  CH_FACTORY_TAG if you do not plan to use abstract serialization in that class (i.e. deserializing objects whose class is not known in advance) because there is a small penalty: this macro introduces a virtual function in your class, so objects will carry a dispatch table with them. For example, there is no need to use it for ChVector.

author: Colin Vanden Heuvel <cvandenheuve@wisc.edu>
message:
Fixes POSIX threads implementation on macOS/OSX

Chrono Parallel relies on an optional feature (memory-based semaphores)
for its implementation of ChThreadsPOSIX. This feature is not available
in Mac (Darwin) based kernels, and causes a "spinning wheel of death" to
appear when demos using it are executed. (tested on macOS Sierra 10.12.3)

This bug has been present for an unknown length of time, and has been
indicated on recent builds with the warning -Wdeprecated-declarations.

Implemented with platform-specific defines, the now-working implementation
uses POSIX named semaphores. This implementation may actually be cross-
platform for UNIX-like systems because it relies only on required
pthreads features, but for the purposes of this feature branch, it will be
only on Apple.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor Chrono iterative solvers (API changes).

- introduce base class ChIterativeSolver which provides basic, common settings for all iterative solvers (both LS and VI).
- all iterative solvers specify maximum number of iterations, a tolerance for stopping criteria, whether or not to use diagonal preconditioning (if supported), and whether or not to use an initial guess (when appropriate)
- all iterative solvers report the actual number of iterations taken for the last solve operation and the "tolerance error" reached during the last solve (its meaning differs from solver to solver).
- ChIterativeSolverLS and ChIterativeSolverVI use double inheritance.
- remove constructor arguments for all iterative VI solvers (use Set methods to change default values).
- update all iterative VI solvers to implement the ChIterativeSolver interface.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New feature: antialiasing in Irrlicht.
The antialiasing is ON by default in ChIrrApp, because on recent HW there is negligible overhead and it runs almost as fast as with no antialiasing.
If you find that the performance of the display driver is worse with antialiasing, you can turn it OFF by using an optional flag in the ChIrrApp constructor, ex from:
ChIrrApp application(&my_system, L"Test", core::dimension2d<u32>(800, 600), false, true);
to
ChIrrApp application(&my_system, L"Test", core::dimension2d<u32>(800, 600), false, true, false);
Note also that demos that use smooth shadow maps require a trick to have antialiasing (as the Irrlicht  Xeffects did not support antialias) so when antialiasing is on, I force the Xeffects buffer to be double the size of the screen buffer, and this gives antialiasing - but please report if this trick has major impact in frame rate of the display.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Fix bug in promoting raw pointer to shared_ptr (use empty destructor).

This issue occurs whenever a raw pointer must be promoted to shared_ptr (e.g. to be passed to some function) but that pointer is already managed through some other shared_ptr.  Without explicitly specifying a custom empty (no-op) destructor, the raw pointer would be deleted when the local (temporary) shared_ptr goes out of scope.

(Note: with the previous ChSharedPtr implementation, this was done by explicitly increasing the reference count of the wrapped ChShared object)

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Provide more flexibility in advancing the state of the multibody system within the Chrono::FSI co-simulation.

- Add option to define a callback class with a custom MBS advance function.
  If no such callback object is defined, ChFsiSystem::DoStepDynamics simply invokes ChSystem::DoStepDynamics (as many times as necessary to advance the multibody system state over the current co-simulation meta-step).
- Add option to disable the integration of the MBS state in ChFsiSystem::DoStepDynamics.
  In this case, it is the caller's responsibility to advance the dynamics of the fluid system (by calling ChFsiSystem::DoStepDynamics) and then the dynamics of the multibody system.

- However, BCE markers are based on collision geometry which itself is relative to the body reference frame.
- Transform local rigid BCE marker positions REF -> ABS -> COM.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor setting and accessing mass and inertia properties of vehicle subsystems (WIP).

- a vehicle subsystem reports its mass, COM frame (relative to the subsystem reference frame), and inertia (relative to its centroidal frame)
- a vehicle subsystem reports its current frame relative to the absolute reference frame
- a subsystem mass is set in the function CalculateMass which is invoked at initialization
- a subsystem updates its inertia, COM frame, and position in the function CalculateInertia which is invoked at the end of a simulation step

- accessor methods for a subsystem mass, COM frame, inertia, and position are provided in the base class ChPart

- tire subsystems must also implement the functions GetAddedMass and GetAddedInertia to indicate quantities that are accumulated on the associated spindle body.  Only deformable tire models return 0.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Redesign use of OpenMP in Chrono.

- ChSystem::SetNumThreads sets the number of OpenMP threads separately and independently for use in Chrono itself (e.g. in FEA internal force and Jacobian evaluation), in collision detection (if using multi-threaded Bullet collision), and in Eigen (for sparse direct solvers).
- Use 'num_threads' clause for parallel omp for loops in FEA.  Similarly, Bullet was modified for Chrono to also use the 'num_threads' clause in its parallel for loops. This implies that the caller *must* invoke ChSystem::SetNumThreads.
- The number of OpenMP threads used by the sparse direct solvers in Chrono::MKL (Pardiso) and Chrono::MUMPS are specified at construction time.
- Chrono::Parallel uses the same number of threads for collision detection and its own parallel solvers.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Important. NEVER use the "using namespace XXYYZZ;"  shortcut in HEADER files, that is: in .h files it is safe to do
  namespace XXYYZZ { ..... etc.. in brackets..
but no "using namespace XXYYZZ;" shortcut, whereas in .cpp files one can do both (usually the 2nd is easier). This means that in certain cases one has to explicitly type all the namespace in .h if the brackets are not possible. Say, for the std:: namespace.
Well, this is expecially true for stl now. You need to write explicitly std::cout  std::min   std::vector etc. in your headers, no cout min vector, got it?.
The reason?
This is even more important now that we started using the official C++11 timing classes, that are in std::chrono - an unlucky case of namespace confusion because we already have our chrono:: here in place.
Hence, if a "using namespace std;" slips in a header, we will have tons of "ambiguous chrono namespace" errors. So, avoiding using XXYYZZ namespace; in headers (something that is always bad in any case) is now even more important because of this std::chrono ambiguity.

author: Mike Taylor <mtaylor22@wisc.edu>
message:
Adding templatized versions of 5 ANCF elements with optimizations for execution speed with the option for a “continuous integration” or “pre-integration” method for the generalized internal force and its Jacobian.  Breakout ANCF Materials into standalone classes.

Added the following 5 ANCF elements:
 - Fully parameterized 2 node beam 3243 (ChElementBeamANCF_3243)
 - Gradient deficient 3 node beam 3333 (ChElementBeamANCF_3333)
 - Fully parameterized 4 node shell 3443 (ChElementShellANCF_3443)
 - Higher order 8 node shell 3833 (ChElementShellANCF_3833)
 - Fully parameterized 8 node brick 3843 (ChElementBrickANCF_3843)

Each element is templatized by the number of Gauss quadrature points used for the generalized internal force vector calculation and its Jacobian.  Default parameters are set for each element that yielded a good balance between performance and accuracy compared to a full number of Gauss quadrature points for each element.

Each element can be set to use either a “continuous integration” or the Liu et al. based “pre-integration” calculation method for the generalized internal force vector.  In most cases, the default “continuous integration” method will likely be faster.  If using shell elements with many discrete layers, then the “pre-integration” method could be faster.  Testing has shown that ChElementBeamANCF_3333 is significantly faster than the existing equivalent ChElementBeamANCF element and ChElementShellANCF_3833 is significantly faster than the existing equivalent ChElementShell_8 element.  As a result, ChElementBeamANCF and ChElementShell_8 might be removed in the future since they are redundant.

Details on the generalized internal force and Jacobian calculations can be found in UW-Madison SBEL Tech Report TR-2020-09 (to be published) <https://sbel.wisc.edu/technicalreports/>

Modified ChElementBeamANCF to use the new standalone ChMatrialBeamANCF class.  This class has code specific to the ChElementBeamANCF which will be removed if ChElementBeamANCF is removed in the future.

author: Marcel Offermans <marrs@xs4all.nl>
message: If you downshifted all the way to neutral with a manual transmission, it would leave the gear in 1st (as gear zero currently means reverse, so there is no proper setting for neutral). However it would change the current gear ratio to a very big number, effectively allowing the engine to rev freely. If you would then upshift into first again, there was a check that would detect you were already in first gear and the ratio would not be changed back. This check now checks if both the gear number and ratio are correct and if either does not, it effectively shifts gears.

Making G mandatory, now none can forget it.

author: Antonio Recuero <recuero@wisc.edu>
message:
Add 3-node continuum-based, fully 3D ANCF beam element.

This element models the internal forces of a beam using a continuum based approach. Poisson locking is avoided by integrating Poisson terms over the beam centerline. This element captures, extension, bending, torsion, and shear deformation. Additionally, the user can select to account for Poisson effect. The initial configuration of the FEA system is automatically considered as the reference. Isotropic and orthotropic materials can be selected. Further details on the features of this ANCF beam element may be found in Nachbagauer, Gruber, and Gerstmayr, "Structural and Continuum Mechanics Approaches for a 3D Shear Deformable ANCF Beam Finite Element:  Application to Static and Linearized Dynamic Examples", Journal of Computational and Nonlinear Dynamics, 2013, April 2013, Vol. 8, 021004.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor functions for adding bodies to a ChSystemDistributed:

- rename IncrementGID to IncrementNumBodiesGlobal
- implement AddBodyTrust which can be used to create and add bodies *only* on those ranks that overlap the initial body location.   This is a lower-level function, in that the user must check the location (using the InSub function) and then call *on all ranks* IncrementNumBodiesGlobal
- change AddBody which can be used to add a body to the system without user intervention.  This function performs its own location checks and adds the body only to the appropriate ranks.  It also increments the global number of bodies.   While potentially slower for systems with large number of bodies, this function allows using various Chrono utilities such as those for generating granular material with an API consistent with Chrono and Chrono::Parallel
- changed AddBodyAllRanks to automatically increment the global body counter

- all demos and tests were modified to use AddBodyTrust, but some can (should) switch to using AddBody

Change the simulation loop to mimic a co-simulation framework.

For now, this is a trivial explicit coupling co-simulation with all modules taking one fixed step equal to the communication interval.
The modules are given a chance to exchange data (by calling their respective Update functions), after which they are simulated to the next time (by calling their respective Advance functions).

Optimization: the Project() function in frictional contact was impacting the solver's timing. This used  up to 8%-10% of SOR time during iterations. (These numbers are for the SOR solver, but also other solvers in general). One overhead happens because of thesqrt function: I moved it later, after earlier rejection tests using squared inequalities, to postpone as much as possible.
This optimization alone reduced about 25% the time spent in Project().

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add option for a simplified double-pin track shoe model which uses a single connector body.

- The track shoe mechanism topology is selected through a constructor argument (of type DoublePinTrackShoeType) which can be TWO_CONECTORS or ONE_CONNECTOR
- When specified through a JSON file, use the key "Topology" with a value "Two Connectors" or "One Connector".  If the "Topology" key is missing, a two-connector double-pin track shoe is constructed
- The TWO_CONNECTORS topology uses two separate connector bodies, one the left and right side of the track
- The ONE_CONNECTOR topology uses a single connector body with collision shapes on its left and right sides
- In both cases, the collision geometry is the same and therefore the same double-pin sprocket can be used

(cherry picked from commit a46b30f056865325f93c7d54afb09bba9e9b23af)

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Intermediate application of tire forces through the wheel object.

- Maintain a back-pointer to the tire attached to a wheel
- Application of tire forces to the suspension spindle bodies is done during wheel synchronization (triggered by the wheeled vehicle)
- This eliminates the need for the user to get the tire forces and pass them to the vehicle system during synchronization
- This allows making ChTire::GetTireForce private
- Important: a tire model should *not* zero out forces during its synchronization, as vehicle synchronization (and hence wheeled synchronization) may occur after tire synchronization.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add option for spoecifying limits to the SCM computational domain.

- By default, the SCM terrain patch extends to infinity in the x-y plane, beyond the area used to initialize it; outside the initialization area, the height of the SCM terrain is that of the closest initialized point.
- If specified, SCM terrain forces outside the boundary are not generated. The boundary is specified as an axis-aligned bounding box expressed relative to the SCM reference.
- This feature is useful in stitching an environment with multiple SCM terrain patches or with a combination of SCM and rigid terrain patches.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add option to calculate nodal direction vectors for FSI flexible meshes (WIP).

- for 1-D FEA mesh geometry (collision segment sets for cables or beams), these are averages of the adjacent segment directions.
- for 2-D mesh geometry (mesh collision surfaces for shells and solid elements), these are averages oif the adjacent face normals.
- this information can be used to obtain a smoother (C1 continuous) reconstruction of the deformed FEA mesh for FSI coupling purposes.
- the SPH solver can use this information to generate better sets of solid BCE markers on flexible solids (TODO).
- if this option is enabled, the generic FSI interface performs the calculation on the CPU (in ChFsiInterface::StoreSolidStates) and communincates it through its staging buffers.
- a concrete fluid solver can overwrite this behavior with a more efficient implementation. In particluar, the Chrono::FSI SPH solver calculates direction vectors on the device.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Important changes in ChSystem.
- The ChAssembly class has been completely redesigned to be parent class of ChSystem
- Many iterations on sub-objects in ChSystem have been ported to parent ChAssembly, to avoid duplicated code
- The ChSystem class has been cleaned: old unused code has been removed / updated
- in ChSystem::Setup() there is an optional sanity check for the bookkeeping , enabled only in _DEBUG mode and with a bool flag. This ensures that all DOFs offsets & counts in all ChPhysicsItem objects are consistent.
- some loops have been parallelized with OpemMP (just experiments, not dynamic scheduling, nor nested).
These changes have been tested and work with all the demos, except with demo_FEAbrick.cpp that halts with a singular matrix.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New constraint: ChShaftsGearboxAngled. It implements a gearbox with given transmission ratio between 1D input and 1D output, but with different directions in 3D space. Basically it defines a transmission ratio between two 1D entities of ChShaft type, and transmits the reaction of the gearbox to a 3D body that acts as the  support truss.
A typical example is the case of a gearbox with bevel gears, where input shaft and output shaft are at 90°.
Note that the more basic ChShaftsGear can do the same, except that it does not provide a way to transmit reaction to a 3D truss body.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add utility functor classes for specifying a spring-damper force with pre-tension.

- these classes implement ChSpringForceCallback to calculate a force:    f - F_spring - F_damper
- LinearSpringDamperActuatorForce uses F_spring = k * (displacement)  and F_damper = c * (velocity), for given f, k, c
- MapSpringDamperActuatorForce uses data to calculate through interpolation F_spring = F(displacement) and F_damper = F(velocity), for given f and curve data
