message:
New classes for Gauss-Legendre quadrature of functions in 1D, 2D, 3D intevals.
Will be used for advanced FEM.
Note that the ChQuadrature class, thanks to templating, can also integrate tensorial/vectorial functions.
The quadrature algorithm is optimized so that, in case of low (<10) order, precomputed polynomial coefficients are used, otherwise, in sake of generality, for larger orders it automatically falls back to just-in-time polynomial table computation.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New constraint type: ChShaftsGearbox. It defines a transmission ratio between two 1D entities of  ChShaft type, and transmits the reaction of the gearbox to a 3D body that acts as the support truss.
Note that the more basic ChShaftsGear can do the same, except that it does not provide a way to transmit reaction to a truss body. This can be useful when simulating vehicles, where some parts of the driveline are gearbox connected to sprung masses, so one might want to capture the 'twist' effect when torque flows in the driveline.
Also note that this can also be seen as a ChShaftPlanetary where one has joined the carrier shaft to a fixed body via a ChShaftsBody constraint.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor setting of solver parameters through ChSystem (API changes).

- given the larger number of solvers available now (LS vs VI, iterative vs direct) and types of problems (NSC vs SMC, DVI vs DAE, etc), providing a ChSystem interface to the underlying solver is limiting.
- the recommended way for attaching a solver is to create the solver object, set parameters, and then associate the solver to the system using ChSystem::SetSolver.
- for backward compatibility and to allow simple demos and tests, ChSystem::SetSolverType is maintained (limited to iterative solvers).
- furthermore, for iterative solvers it is still possible to set the two main parameters (maximum number of iterations and tolerance) directly through ChSystem methods (SetSolverMaxIterations and SetSolverTolerance, respectively).
- all other solver settings (omega and lambda for PSOR-like solvers, use of diagonal preconditioning, etc) require access to the solver object.
- note also that, for consistency and correctness, the ChSystem methods directly invoke the corresponding ChIterativeSolver method (in other words, ChSystem does not maintain separate variables for the maximum number of iterations or for the tolerance level, as this may lead to iconsistencies).
- having said that, this functionality should be eventually deprecated and eliminated.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor Chrono::Parallel to support addition of contacts through a user-provided callback.

- Add specializations of ChContactContainerParallel for NSC and SMC contacts.
- These derived classes implement the AddContact function that does not rely on collision shapes (callable from user-provided collision callbacks), as well as an internal helper function to add a compute the composite material properties for a collision identified by the underlying collision detection system, given the global indices of the colliding bodies and shapes.  Derived parallel collision containers work with contact method-specific arrays in the global data structure.
- Move all calculations related to computing and loading composite material properties in ChCollisionSystemParallel::ReportContacts, so that these can occur before processing any user-provided collision callback.
- This new computational flow matches more closely the one done in the core Chrono library.
- Add demo_PAR_custom_contact to illustrate the use of a custom collision callback.

Note:  For SMC contact method, a custom collision callback cannot currently be used with the MultiStep tangential displacement model;  this is because MultiStep requires knowledge of the indices of colliding shapes which are not created when adding custom contacts.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add new translational spring-damper-actuator force element.

- replacement for ChLinkSpring and ChLinkSpringCB
- derived directly from ChLink (simpler and more streamlined implementation not using the heavier ChLinkMarkers)
- like ChLinkSpringCB, allows user-specified force definition (through a callback mechanism)
- default (no user-provided force functor) is a linear spring-damper
- may have internal dynamics (ODEs specified through a callback mechanism) which are integrated with the containing system; internal states can be used in force calculation
- provides support for calculating the full Jacobian (w.r.t. states of connected bodies and, if present, internal states)

message:
Fix powertrain maps to address a quirk in the current ChSimpleMapPowertrain implementation.

If the powertrain maps are such that they give exactly zero torque at zero speed, it's possible to get stuck and not be able to move the vehicle.
This can occur if the shaft speed has a negative value and we are in a forward gear (in which case the calculated motor speed is clamped to 0).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Partial fix for Windows DLL issue for Python v > 3.8.

Starting with version 3.8, Python no longer uses the PATH environment variable on Windows to look for DLLs.
Instead, it requires *all* necessary DLLs to be copied next to the python module or else using of the os.add_dll_directory() function.
The first in a non-option for a module such as Cascade which requires all OCC DLLs.
The solution in this commit (based on the 2nd option above) resolves the problem for the Sensor module (which only requires some of the CUDA DLLs) but is only a partial solution for the Cascade module (the OCC DLLs should be visible now, but not the DLLs for other OCC dependencies)

New demo: demo_FEAcosimulate_load.
This explains how to use the new feature "ChLoadContactSurfaceMesh" to exchange data from/to an external process that computes applied nodal forces to a triangle mesh (ex. it could be a SPH, a CFD, a DVI simulation of a soil, etc.).
The demo is intentionally simple - the external process just computes a bed of  spring-damper arrays, and cosimulation is simulated by calling a simple function from the same .cpp file, but nothing prevents using MPI and using external machines.

Add mechanism to disable self-collisions for a ChContactSurface (node cloud or trimesh).

By default, self-collision are allowed and included in collision detection.
If appropriate for a given simulation, these can be disabled by specifying a collision family for the contact surface.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: Change the formula for incremental update of state (rotation part). Previusly, it went through a complex sequence (convert of angluar increment from local to absolute, transform into angle-axis, conversion to quaternion, etc.), now it exploits the fact that it can be done in a single quaternion product as  q_new = q_old * delta_q_local, and this is equivalent to  q_new = delta_q_absolute * q_old . This also saves the Amatrix* multiplication, that was referencing an internal data of the body/node/etc. and this was not correct because the StateIncrement function assumes to be independent on actual configuration of the object.

Add base class for a mobilized body (SOA-based recursive dynamics).

- ChMobilizedBody defines an articulated body, part of a multibody subassembly speficied in relative coordinates.
- The ChMobilizedBody base class declares the main outward (base-to-tip) and inward (tip-to-base) recursive operators for forward and inverse dynamics.
- ChMassProps defines body inertial properties as spatial matrices.
- ChMobilityForce defines hinge forces acting on a single degree of freedom.
- ChSoaAssembly is the container class representing a subassembly modeled in recursive dynamics which will be available as a Chrono modeling component.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New feature: ChSystem::SetDumpMatrices().
If you enable  SetDumpMatrices(true), for each solver call during the simulation, the system will dump matrices and vectors on the disk, with the following format:
  solve_0001_01_M.dat     solve_0001_01_Cq.dat    etc.
  solve_0002_01_M.dat     solve_0002_01_Cq.dat    etc.
In general:
  solve_<number_of_step>_<number_of_solver_call>_<data_name>.dat
where number_of_solver_call can be >1 in those cases (ex. HHT solver) that require more than a single solve per timestep.
Later those files can be quickly load in Matlab using the uitlity function that I just sent to GIT as:
   chrono/data/load_system_matrices.m
Note: one can esily turn on/off this logging by pressing the F7 key in the Irrlicht interface.

message:
Split copying of sorted marker data to original ordering based on marker group (type of SPH marker).

- copy data in original order for SPH particles and BCE boundary markers (i.e., all "non-solid" markers) after advancing dynamics of the fluid phase.
- copy data in original order for BCE markers on rigid and flexible objects (i.e., all "solid" markers) after updating states of solid phase.
- allows using the fluid solver by itself (i.e., not through a ChFsiSystem) for problems that only involve the fluid phase.
- fixes marker issues with the new timing of data exchange between phases in the concurrent FSI system DoStepDynamics.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Modifications to CMake build system:

1. Use FindChronoEngine.cmake
    This needs some improvements (in particular, rely on Chrono package configuration files so that we do not have to duplicate work already done when Chrono was configured).
    We require that Chrono was built with unit_POSTPROCESS enabled.
    We optionally enable Irrlicht support in chrono-T (but if we do, it is assumed that Chrono was built with unit_IRRLICHT enabled.  However, since unit_IRRLICHT is not yet a separate DLL, there is no check for this.)

2. Under Windows, use CMake custom target and commands to copy the required DLLs as a post-build operation.  With these changes:
    - there is no need to rerun CMake for chrono-T if the Chrono libraries change
    - there is no need to select the configuration type (e.g., Debug, Release, etc) when configuring chrono-T in CMake
    - the appropriate DLLs are copied in the appropriate directory when building the chrono-T solution. Of course, the Chrono DLLs corresponding to the currently selected Build type must exist.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Remove setting 'use_material_props' from all Chrono::Vehicle deformable tires.

- this is a system-level setting, affecting all containing contactable physical items and as such inappropriate to be set by a tire component.
- instead, a particular ChDeformableTire must provide all required parameters (whether material properties or coefficients) so that it can be used no matter how the system is set up.
- default values for both material properties and contact coefficients are provided at construction and user-callable methods allow changing either group from their default values.
- a JSON specification file can optionally contain the groups "Properties" and/or "Coefficients" to modify the default values for material properties and contact coefficients, respectively.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: Redesigned storage metho for eigenvalue analysis. The function ComputeModes() and ComputeModesDamped() functions can be called even after an assembly has been converted into a reduced modal assembly via SwitchModalReductionON(). Previously these two functions worked only for unreduced assembly. In this way now we can treat the reduced modal assembly as a black box for whome we may be interested in getting eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Results of these Compute functions go into dedicated data structures that won't be used later even if after a SwitchModalReductionON.

message:
Feature/granular (#268)

Updates and fixes to Chrono::Granular

* bug fix, correct unit in force output

* bug fix in advance_simulation

* change shearband demo name

* modify shear_band demo name to movingBoundary

* modify cmakelist

* record contact force info

* add API

* fixed bug 1: triangle soup need proper initialization in initializeTriangles(); and bug 2: angular acceleration calculation typo

* added the api to specify initial angular velocities of spheres

* a typo fix

* error handling

* attempting (1) to that fix SD--triangle bug

* api for initializing pos, velo, angvelo

* optimized the calculation of SD center in GPU_SMC_trimesh; mixer demo added for the tutorial

* add API

* add API to get position of BC plane

* implementation for returning BC plane position

* bug fix: use frictional contact for cylinder BC

* bug fix: typo in calculation of distance from sphere to cylinder boundary

* change v_rot threshold comparison to user unit

In Schwartz's implementation of rolling friction model, the torque
is calculated as mu_r * R * (F_N v_rot)/|v_rot|. When particle is
supposed to settle due to rolling resistance, rolling torque does
not dissipate, instead, it flucates between two small values causing
unwanted oscillation/creep in the particle. A quick fix is to set
rolling resistance to zero when v_rot is less than a threshol value.

* Fix some bugs in rolling friction calculation of sphere and mesh

* Fix a bug in the calculation of relative ang. vel. between mesh and particle

* Make mass unit conversion accessible in unified memory

* print error info on BD and global pos when particles move outside BD

* Clean up

* Change the mixer demo to use the internal bladed mixer

* Add demo for compression test

* Add json input for compression test

* Add api for return number of sphere-sphere contacts

* Clean up; nice print out for error message; modify cmake list

* Added Granular repose demo

* JSON File for repose demo renamed

* Update json input file for fixed terrain

* Added python post-processing utility for normal and friction network visualization

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add ChBody functions to report the resultant applied force and torque, respectively.

- This information requires computing a system-wide of (unscaled) generalized forces from which the applied force and torque for a given body can be extracted.
- To prevent additional overhead when this information is not requested (the common case), we use lazy evaluation.
- As such, the cost of one call to ChSystem::LoadResidual_F is added at any time when at least one call to ChBody::GetAppliedForce or ChBody::AppliedTorque is made.  However, this cost is independent of the number of bodies for which the query is made at *that* particular time.
- This cost is not incurred for Chrono::Parallel (where this information is already cached).
- Note that the reported forces and torques *do not* include any constraint forces (in particular, for the NSC formulation they *do not* include the contact forces).

- Mixer demos (both NSC and SMC, both sequential and parallel) were modified to illustrate the use of these functions (uncomment the relevant code within the simulation loops).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Support composite inertia properties in JSON specification for a Chrono::Vehicle chassis.

The inertia properties of the chassis rigid body is calculated for a collection of sub-systems (all assumed rigidly attached to the chassis body).

Each sub-system is specified through a centroidal frame (relative to the chassis reference frame), a mass, moments of inertia (w.r.t. the sub-component's centroidal frame), and product of inertia (w.r.t. the sub-component's centroidal frame).  Optionally, a sub-component can be marked as a "void", in which case its inertia properties are subtracted from that of the composite.  Note that products of inertia are assumed to include the minus sign; in other words, the provided 3-dimensional vector should contain [ -int{xy}dm   -int{xz}dm   -int{yz}dm ]

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
This commit adds the possibility of making N simulation substeps each rendering step.
In fact the 3D refresh might be overkill if running at 1kHz simulation step. Usually, 50 fps is enough for video refresh.
Example, here it makes 20 simulation steps each video refresh, so -optimally- the video should run a 50fps and the simulation loop at 1kHz (if the cpu power is enough.)
Note that if using the realtime stepping system, as SetTryRealtime(true), this might end in having the last dt integration step in each N substeps longer than the others, because the time wasted in the loop includes also the video refresh. I guess...
The realtime stepping system should be improved anyway.

message: Bug fix. The ChLinkMotorRotationDriveline included some sub-objects of ChPhysics type. The output of GetOffset_w() and GetOffset_x() gave wrong results because their offsets were never shifted by parent's offset during Setup(). The result is that the code worked in most cases, except when a ChShaftTorsionalSpringDamper was added, operating on one of the two ineer shafts, beause it needs GetOffset_w(). So, a bookkeeping error caused the torque to be applied to a wrong coordinate, leading to wrong results.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Chrono::Parallel NSC: use contact materials from collisding shapes.

- for each contact, create and use a composite material based on the materials of colliding shapes (not bodies) for all rigid-rigid contacts
- eliminate global arrays with NSC material properties, except for those holding sliding coefficients of friction and (constant) cohesion
- these values are only used for fluid-rigid and FEA-rigid contacts and are currently set from the contact material of the first collision shape in the body collision model

Note: use shared_ptr even if in a parallel for loop (control block is thread safe).   To revisit passing by value vs. passing by reference.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Major updates to the IGA beam. Now it is working OK. There are some remainig features, but the bulk of the work is done.
Important news:
- the internal force computation has been split in ComputeInternalForces(), which uses the current state, and ComputeInternalForces_impl(), that uses a generic state.
- the internal force computation had some bugs in rotation interpolations, now fixed
- the stiffness matrix is implemented with a brute force approach, using numerical differentiation. Maybe not 100% elegant, but it works fine so far.
- implemented the interfaces for ChLoadableU, for applying distributed loads, if wanted, and for helping with the stiffness matrix computation via numerical differentiation
- implemented some experimental code for structural damping a-la-Raleygh, in the internal force computation. But please do not use it for the moment  (i.e. set Raleygh damping to 0) because the computation of the damping matrix is not yet in place

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
MAJOR refactoring:
the new class ChBodyFrame has been inserted 'in between' ChFrame and ChBody.
This class ChBodyFrame has been used also as a base for some FEM nodes (namely, those for end-rotations of beams, i.e. nodes that have the same 6 dofs as the rigid bodies). The new class defines basic interface to simulation items with 6dofs, but it is more lightweight than the full ChBody.
The nice side effect is that one will be able to use constraints on both ChBody objects and ChNodeFEMxyzrot objects, to join beam trusses and rigid bodies, for instance using the constraints in the ChLinkMate classes.
The drawback is that lot of classes needed some refactoring.

Adds GCC version checking to CMakeLists.txt for Chrono::FSI

Modern GCC uses C++14 by default, which conflicts with CUDA. In order to
enable CUDA support on modern GCC, -std=c++11 must be passed to the host
compiler by nvcc. This appears is only valid if CUDA_HOST_COMPILER is
GCC 5.4.

Also adds slightly more complex version checking to Chrono::Parallel,
allowing users to manually enable USE_PARALLEL_CUDA if they know their
CUDA_HOST_COMPILER to be compatible.

The changes build successfully on GCC 5.4.0 (and GCC 6.2.1 with
-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=/path/to/gcc-5) and CUDA 8.0 with various
combinations of ENABLE_MODULE_FSI, ENABLE_MODULE_IRRLICHT,
ENABLE_MODULE_PARALLEL, ENABLE_MODULE_VEHICLE, and USE_PARALLEL_CUDA.

message: New function  ChBlender::SetRank(int) . When doing simulations or cosimulations with multiple compute nodes in parallel, each using its own ChBlender exporter, there is the risk that they generate the same ID for name of Blender shapes (assuming you use the Blender plugin in "Merge" mode). So you can use SetRank() with unique integer per each node: this doing, each Blender shape will be prefixed by ..._n_ where n is the rank number, and there won't be any name conflict.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Fix functions for calculating element contributions to nodal generalized forces.

This allows a given element to use derived node classes (e.g. a ChNodeFEAxyzD instead of ChNodeFEAxyz) where appropriate to permit different element types to share nodes in the same mesh.
The fix involves asking a given element for the number of nodal coordinates it affects for a given node (instead of asking the node itself for its total number of coordinates) while including the contributions to the nodal generalized forces.

Limitations:  an element always adds its contribution to the first coordinates of its adjacent nodes.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Modify implementation of collision families to use bit masks.

For consistency with the bullet collision system, we use (signed) shorts to hold the collision family (encoded in 'family_group' as a power of 2, with the position of the set bit indicating the family) and the collision mask (encoded in 'family_mask' with a set bit indicating collision with the corresponding family).

This limits the number of collision families to one of the following 15 values: {0, 1, ..., 14}.  Note that we use signed shorts so we must be careful with the sign bit.

A "no collision" relationship is commutative but not transitive.  Note that, unless explicitly changed, the bit in a model's mask corresponding to the model's own family is set.  As such, this should not be relied upon to ignore self-collisions.

Collision family information in this format is now saved and retrieved from checkpoint files.  This invalidates previous checkpoint files which should be regenerated.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New important feature: the 'particlefactory' namespace & source directory.
This directory contains new classes for generating flows of particles, with random shapes, positions, alignments, etc.
Each randomized feature (shape, size, etc.) can be defined using one or more distributions from the recent ChDistribution.h collection, ex the normal distribution, the Weibull distribution, the exponential distribution, discrete distributions, etc.
This extremely modular approach can be used to generate infinite types of mixtures.
Nte that this is still a work in progress; in future I'll merge also Radu's code for creating volumes filled with particles.
Things to do: make the generator 'templated' so that one can also generate GPU bodies or who knows in future, and also add a ChParticleGenerator of the type 'generate from particle samples', that will clone sample particles (but sharing their visual assets and the collision shapes, to save memory!!).
Also, add more demos.

- internal CUDA files and classes have no prefix nor suffix.

- rename `ChFsiForceExplicitSPH` to `FsiForceWCSPH` and `ChFsiForceI2SPH` to `FsiForceISPH`.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Added geometric stiffness matrix for Euler-Bernoulli beams, previously neglected (nonlinear dynamics was ok anyway, but if one extracted M and K system-wide matrices for doing modal analyisis, the frequencies could be slightly underestimated  when beams were in pre-stressed state. Now stretched beams have an increase in lateral stiffness in the tangent stiffness matrix, like it happens in guitar strings. Again, for time stepping it was almost the same because time integrators converged anyway, but for dumping K matrices for modal analyis, this makes a difference).
Turned on by default. Can be disabled via ChElementBeamEuler::SetUseGeometricStiffness(false).

message:
Major change in the interface to LCP solver technology.
Previously, solvers had a boolean flag in Solve(..) to ask that the [M]*v_old  term was added to the known term (forces, etc.) .
Now this is not needed anymore, because the LCPprepare_load() function in ChSystem will take care of this, thank to the new
functions VariablesFbIncrementMq() that have been added to all ChPhysicsItem objects.
The reason: this is required for the new FEM technology in unit_FEM.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
IMPORTANT change in ChQuaternion API.  Previously, the * operator was used for doing element-by-element product, that was almost useless. We assume that no one used it. So, now we use the * operator to perform the true quaternion operator, as it was done with % operator previously.
The old % operator is made deprecated, then.
Also, we added the >> operator and its in-place >>= operator, to do the product in 'specular' order, i.e. A*B is the same as B >> A.
This makes things more coherent through the Chrono::ENgine API because the * operator represents the same 'meaning' also for ChFrame, ChFrameMoving, etc. , that is, it 'concatenates' transformations in direct order (in this cases, for quaternion it concatenates rotations). Similarly, the >> operator provides a concatenation of transformations in specular order.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add functions to enable (allow) brake locking for all concrete wheeled vehicle models.

- for uniformity and backward compatibility, brake locking is disabled by default
- Attention: brake locking should *not* be enabled when using rigid tires (as the locking of joints can negatively interfere with the Chrono contact, especially for the NSC formulation)
- In general, brake locking should be enabled for all other tire models (TMeasy, Fiala, Pacejka) as this helps with stopping on an incline

Refactor creation and initialization of Chrono::Vehicle subsystem (ChPart).

- Make Initialize() functions non-virtual.
- Change signature of ChTrackShoe::Initialize to take as first argument a ChChassis (and not a ChBodyAuxRef).
- The base class Initialize() function, for each vehicle subsystem, (1) sets the parent part and a tag for bodies created by the part, (2) invoke a virtual function Construct() which creates the concrete subsystem, and (3) performs generic additional calculations (if any).
- The body tag encodes a vehicle tag (unique identifier for each vehicle in a simulation) and a tag for the specific vehicle subsystem.
- This allows (1) identifying vehicle subsystems at run-time (e.g., for controlling visibility during rendering), as well as subsystem type (e.g., for contact management)

Optimization. The ChContactContainerNSC and ChContactContainerSMC spent too much time in AddContact because some dynamic_cast<> took too much time in the dispatcher that switches between types of contact pairs. Therefore, now we dispatch by avoiding dynamic_cast; this uses a virtual function with much smaller overhead, returning an enum that is a shortcut for  rtti info.
This optimization alone reduced about 50% the time spent in AddContacts, giving a 5%-10% speedup in total execution time for contact intensive tests.

message:
Fix an issue where VS compilation of the Chrono_fsisph library generated a large number of warnings.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
HHT: switch to relative + absolute NR convergence test (in POSITION mode).

NR is declared converged if the WRMS norm of the update is less than 1.
The WRMS norm test is a relative + absolute tolerance test:
    ||v||_WRMS = sqrt{ sum{(v_i * w_i}^2 / N }
where the weights are calculated as
    w_i = 1 / (reltol * |v0_i| + abstol)
with v0 the current solution (i.e., the solution at previous step).
WRMS norms for the updates in positions and Lagrange multipliers are calculated separately and use possibly different absolute tolerances.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
The lumped mass matrix for FEA with Euler beams (new formulation introduced one month ago) was rank deficient because zero inertia was associated with the rotational degrees of freedom. Previously was 1/50 of the mass per unit length.
Note: the Euler beam with lumped mass could do without this term, however:
1)  differently from Cosserat / IGA element    this inertia contribution reflects the fact that if an Euler beam node rotates, also the centerline wobbles up & down, so mass distributed along centerline far from the section affects the rotation, literature tells that there is no optimal unique way to fix this in a lumped mass context,  and
2)  the Euler beam assumes that mass is concentrated along the centerline as a point on a section, whereas the Cosserat / GEBM / IGA / Timoshenko-Ehrenfest beam / Reynolds beams consider the fact that mass is distributed on a wide section. Among the two issues, the first is the most important here, because the option of setting zero rotational inertia causes mass matrix to be singular - a problem when doing modal analysis.
Now there is a method  SetArtificialJzzJyy_factor()  that can be used to set rotational lumped inertia as   Jzz=Jyy=factor*(mass per unit lenght). Note that even using zero is ok for implicit simulations (the denser the mesh, the less the effect of this artificial term, anyway), but for modal analysis etc. you might need this. Default is 1./500. of the mass per unit lenght.

- ChWheeledVehicle::GetWheelbase() is required (pure virtual function).  For JSON-specified vehicles, if the key "Wheelbase" is not provided, the wheelbase is calculated as the distance between the first and last axles.

- ChVehicle::GetMinTurningRadius() returns a default value of 20 m.   A concrete class should override this with a more accurate value.
- ChVehcile::GetMaxSteeringAngle() has a default implementation which estimates the maximum wheel steering angle from a bicycle model using the turning radius, wheelbase, and wheel track.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor integration step for the Chrono SPH solver.

- rewrite the main kernel for SPH integration to separate the Euler steps for the different states (position, velocity, density, tau).
- this kernel can be used for the existing RK-2 integration scheme (2 calls) or for a standard explicit Euler step (1 call).
- the different device functions for the different states can be used to assemble other integration schemes (TODO).
- replace FluidDynamics::IntegrateSPH with Advance*** functions which clearly reveal the different integration schemes.

Other changes:
- add option to enable or disable checking for errors after executing CUDA kernels (default: enabled).
- if enabled, perform checks through thrust::any_of (currently implemented only in FluidDynamics.cu).

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Change in the PovRay exporter.
The fact that an object must be exported or not does not depends anymore on the old system of having it inserted in the POVray exporter list (that was limiting in some cases, and not coherent with other exporters).
So, now, one can flag that an object must be rendered by adding the new ChPovRayAsset (it is just a lightweight asset that acts as a flag).
IT is still backward compatible because I modified the Add() function accordingly.
Note that one reason for this change is that it should be able to accomodate the situation where particles / objects are deleted in the course of the simulation, and the POV exporter will handle this automatically.
BTW Last minute update: this 'deletion' feature is broken. Must be tested/fixed.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
Support for solver warm starting, reusing constraint & contact forces. This exploits persistent information of reaction forces in contacts, that was already implemented in old Chrono versions, but removed since we switched to the new ChIntegrator-based bookkeeping. Now this is working again.
NOTE: this is not supported in all timesteppers. Actually, it is tested for the Euler implicit linearized (the default timestepper, used also for non-smooth dynamics).
NOTE: I expected improvements on the convergence of CCP solvers, instead the benefit is appreciable only in few cases - actually, in some other cases (see bricks demo) the warm starting triggers a more chaotic pattern of forces in time. Should be investigated.

message:
Properly account for the offset and orientation of a visual asset.

A ChVisualization asset defines a transform from the parent (a node in the case of the Irrlicht interface) to the asset.  This must be concatenated with the transform from the asset to the geometry.  Previously, only the latter was accounted for.

Note: I only fixed the sphere, cylinder, and box visual assets.  I still need to look at ChObjShapeFile and ChTriangleMeshShape.

Fix order of synchronization in wheeled vehicle FMU.

It is critical to synchronize the wheels of the vehicle FMU *after* synchronizing the vehicle system itself.
This is because the vehicle FMU does not include tires and, as such, tire/terrain forces are explicitly applied to the wheel bodies.
If this is based on using the wheel body force accumulators, those are cleared during vehicle (suspension) synchronization which therefore must occur *before* tire/terrain forces are included.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New update formula for positions of the HHT stepper, in POSITION mode.
This avoids the   Vnew += (Xnew - X) ..  part that required addition of Lie group elements (ex. quaternions)  to Lie algebra elements (ex. angular velocities), that failed in fact when using rigid bodies, that have 7 dofs vs 6 dofs in position/speeds.
The idea is that (Xnew- X) is anyway a small delta, that is better represented with a Lie algebra element. By splitting Xnew = X + dX where X is Lie group and dX is Lie algebra, one updates dX+=Da (two algebras, ex 6 vs 6 dofs) and later one has Xnew = X+Dx (7 dof = 7 dof incremented by 6 dofs using the quaternion exponential automatically invoked by the + overloaded operator that acts when doing   Lie group + Lie algebra).
This said, anyway, I see that the solver in position mode behaves strangely when using constraints, even if when using same dofs for pos and speed.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Use ChLinkSpringCB for the spring and shock force elements in a ChDoubleWishbone suspension.

This provides greater flexibility and allows for nonlinear spring and/or dampers.
By default we use two internal functor classes which implement linear springs and dampers, respectively, using the coefficients specified through getSpringCoefficient() and getDampingCoefficient(); this is equivalent to the previous behavior.  Optionally, a derived class can use a custom implementation for either force element.  This must be specified by overriding useNonlinearSpring() and/or useNonlinearShock() to return true and providing custom functor classes through getSpringForceCallback() and getShockForceCallback(), respectively.

The new system required a lot of changes in the ChLCP... classes and in other parts of the code.

message:
change v_rot threshold comparison to user unit

In Schwartz's implementation of rolling friction model, the torque
is calculated as mu_r * R * (F_N v_rot)/|v_rot|. When particle is
supposed to settle due to rolling resistance, rolling torque does
not dissipate, instead, it flucates between two small values causing
unwanted oscillation/creep in the particle. A quick fix is to set
rolling resistance to zero when v_rot is less than a threshol value.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Extend SCM to take into account the Bekker parameter Kc.

- this was ignored in previous implementation (always set to 0).
- the characteristic length b in the term Kc/b in Bekker's formula is approximated here as b* = 2 * A / P, where A is the contact patch area and P its perimeter.
- the contact patch is obtained as the 2D convex hull of the projections onto the reference SCM plane of the ray-hit points in a connected island.
- connected islands (individual contact patches) are computed using a flood-filling method.
- each ray-hit point uses the b* value calculated using the area and perimeter of the contact patch it belongs to.

author: tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New feature in Irrlicht viewer. When pressing the F12 key, a directory "povray_project" is immediately created on disk, and .pov .ini .assets etc. files are created inside it, so that later you can use POVray to load the .ini and render the simulation with high quality ray tracing. The Irrlicht visualization might slow down because at each frame the POVray exporter generates files on disk. Press F12 again to stop saving the POVray files. Note that you must later edit the "povray_project/render_frames.pov" to change/add the lights, global illumination, and other specific raytracing settings.
This feature is available only if you build also the POSTPROCESS module, so check *both* ENABLE_MODULE_IRRLICHT and  ENABLE_MODULE_POSTPROCESSING in CMake.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
IMPORTANT. In previous versions of the code, the mphysicalSystem.SetMaxPenetrationRecoverySpeed(...); parameter had effect only if using ZERO compliance in contacts, i.e. the default contact model. When using a non-zero compliance, the max recovery speed parameter had no effect. The reason is that, for nonzero compliance, it starts to clamp also the reaction force, hence in such case it is not just a 'speed recovery limit', but also makes the contact softer. This said, however, for very stiff contact (ie. nonzero SMALL compliances, tending to zero), one was expecting almost the same behavior of ZERO compliance, but the fact that the 'sped recovery limit' kicks in only at zero compliance and not, say, for 1e-20, was quite confusing and not coherent.
Therefore, now this parameter ALWAYS operates on the contact residual: so
- if the compliance is very small, it behaves as for compliance =0, as expected,
- as the compliance grows, it starts to loose its original meaning of "limit of penetration recovery speed" and becomes more and more an heuristic parameter that limits also the contact force; the user should then USE LARGER VALUE of SetMaxPenetrationRecoverySpeed if using LARGER compliance if he does not want to see contacts become numerically softer (or it can be made not active by setting to extremely large values, ex 1e10).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Modifications and bug fixes to HHT.

1. Added support for reducing the stepsize when NR is taking too many iterations
 - multiple internal smaller steps ("microsteps") may be taken in order to advance the solution by the required step
 - an exception is thrown if the step decreases below a user-specified limit (default 1e-10)
 - a stepsize increase can only occur if NR performs well over a user-specified number of microsteps (default: at least 5 microsteps requiring at most 3 NR iterations each)
 - a stepsize increase can only happen at the beginning of a step (not a microstep)
 - factors for stepsize decrease and increase are user-specified (default: 0.5 and 2.0)

2. Fixed convergence criteria for mode=POSITION
 - fixed the threshold solution norm for switching between relative tolerance test and absolute tolerance test.  Since currently we have a single value for tolerance which here is used both as relative and absolute tolerance, the  correct threshold value is 1.0 (in general, this should be approximately rtol/atol)
- included missing scaling factor in the estimation of the Lagrange multiplier update.  Without this, when scaling is enabled, the errors in Lagrange multipliers are grossly underestimated, leading to premature termination of the NR iterations.

message:
Add option for a simplified double-pin track shoe model which uses a single connector body.

- The track shoe mechanism topology is selected through a constructor argument (of type DoublePinTrackShoeType) which can be TWO_CONECTORS or ONE_CONNECTOR
- When specified through a JSON file, use the key "Topology" with a value "Two Connectors" or "One Connector".  If the "Topology" key is missing, a two-connector double-pin track shoe is constructed
- The TWO_CONNECTORS topology uses two separate connector bodies, one the left and right side of the track
- The ONE_CONNECTOR topology uses a single connector body with collision shapes on its left and right sides
- In both cases, the collision geometry is the same and therefore the same double-pin sprocket can be used

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Modify FEA bookkeeping to take into account nodes and elements with potentially fixed DOFs.

Note that implementation of the various FEA element functions still assumes that containers (vector and matrices) sized for the full set of element DOFs are provided.
All bookkeeping is done at the mesh level.  While this may be slightly less efficient than requesting each concrete FEA element to load minimum-size vectors and matrices, it simplifies implementation of new elements which need not care about potentially fixed DOFs.
The assumption is that all active (not fixed) DOFs of an FEA node are contiguous at the beginning of the node variable list.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add option to specify ChDoubleWishbone body inertia matrices in a vehicle-aligned centroidal frame.

- Inertia matrices for the upright and the lower and upper control arms can be provided either in the body centroidal frame (default) or else in a centroidal frame aligned with the vehicle reference frame
- The latter option can be specified through an optional constructor argument (default: false)
- For a double wishbone suspension specified through a JSON file, the default can be changed by setting the key "Vehicle-Frame Inertia" to "true"
- If a JSON specification file does not contain the above key/value pair, the inertia matrices are assumed to be in the body centroidal frame

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add ChAIDriver, a Chrono::Vehicle driver for coupling with an autonomy stack.

- the current implementation assumes that the AI controls are: longitudinal acceleration, front wheel angle, and rear wheel angle (based on a bicycle model with Ackermann steering geometry)
- the input longitudinal acceleration is converted into a target speed and an underlying PID speed controller sets the throttle and braking inputs to match that speed.
- conversion of the input front and rear wheel angles into a steering input (in [-1,1]) is deferred to derived classes which are vehicle-dependent (e.g. using the maximum possible steering angle)
- AIDriver is a derived class which sets driver parameters from a JSON specification file; in this case, a mapping from front wheel angle (in rad) to steering input must be provided

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor logic in adding FSI solids to a ChFsiSystem:

- defer processing of FSI solids to the initialization of the associated FSI fluid solver (this permits taking into account nodal directions for flex solids if in use).
- obsolete ChFsiFluidSystem virtual methods OnAddFsiBody, OnAddFsiMesh1D, and OnAddFsiMesh2D.
- instead, pass the lists of FSI solids to the fluid solver initialization function.
- for the concrete SPH fluid solver, this means that BCE markers on solids are not generated when the solids are added to the system, but rather when the SPH solver is initialized.
- provide for passing rigid geometry associated with an FSI rigid body (a concrete fluid solver may use that to create coupling to solid phase, or else expect geometry to be specified separately).

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Fix issues with calling SetPos, SetRot, and SetCoordsys on a ChBodyAuxRef object.

- These functions modify the centroidal frame of the underlying body.
- For a ChBodyAuxRef, these functions must also adjust the reference frame (relative to the absolute coordinate system), as part of the rigid body resulting movement.
- Note that ref_to_abs is updated to reflect the current centroidal frame pose as part of ChBodyAuxRef::Update, but that is not enough when SetPos or SetRot are called by the user.

Finally, note that this is a temporary solution. The proper fix, which will be implemented later, requires a better, more consistent and intuitive, definition of body frame access functions in the public API.

message:
Note that the inheritance from ChShared has been changed from normal
   public ChShared
into
   public virtual ChShared
because there are more than one class that inherits from ChShared, and some other classes that have multiple inheritance from them, so it creates the famous 'diamond' problem of multiple inheritance.
Using 'virtual' fixes the problem forever.
 I hope this has no impact on performance because the Ref() and Unref() calls in ChShared items, called by shared pointers,  now become virtual.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message: Fix the trouble with SCM and HHT where the slipping was causing reversed traction forces: the reason is that the Update() function was called multiple times in HHT, and only the 1st caused the evaluation of contact forces. But the 1st call to Update() in HHT does not make sense in terms of system state, accidentally speeds were reversed at that point. Removing the optimization that prevented multiple calls to Update did not fix the problem. So now we fix the problem by moving the computation of SCM soil forces in the Setup() call (that happens only at the beginning of each timestep! unlike the Update() )  and now it works. The only issue is that a multistep integrator would like to evaluate varying forces during a single timestep, whereas SCM forces will remain constant in this case, so the convergence properties of some integrators might be wasted.

message:
Modify initialization of wheeled vehicle suspension subsystems to properly accommodate the possible presence of a subchassis.

- Pass pointers to a chassis, a subchassis (possibly null), and a steering (possible null)
- A particular suspension template can access the required connection bodies on any of these subsystems, depending on whether or not the suspension is steered and whether or not the suspension can attach to a subchassis
- If null is passed for the subchassis, the suspension should attach itself to the provided chassis
- If null is passed for the steering, the suspension should set itself as non-steered and attach tierods to the chassis

Currently, only the ChLeafSpringAxle suspension template allows for a subchassis.  All other simply ignore that argument.

author: Colin Vanden Heuvel <cvandenheuve@wisc.edu>
message:
Replaces many math.h includes with cmath

This change fixes some issues with newer compilers (confirmed in gcc 5.4.0)
where calls to math functions throw strange errors regarding them not
being members of namespace std.

Declarations of C standard library functions such as `round()` or
`cos()` in the std:: namespace are not guaranteed in math.h, but are in
cmath. Likewise, C++11's generic integral templates for C math functions
may or may not be defined in math.h, but are guaranteed by cmath.

I tried to make sure that I didn't touch third party includes, only
headers and sources using the chrono:: namespace should be affected.

New. The ChMesh has a new optional feature: it automatically applies gravitational load to all ChLoadableUVW - inherited objects that are contained within.

It inherits the G value in the parent ChSystem.
It reuses a single ChLoad object that is iterated over all elements, to save memory, rather than connecting tons of ChLoad objects to tons of elements.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Redesign Chrono Bezier curve class to properly construct closed-loop curves.

- pass constructor argument indicating whether or not the loop should be closed (default false)
- if constructing from spline, set up appropriate BC (C1 continuity) for a closed-loop path; solve resulting system using Eigen::SparseLU (not a tridiagonal system anymore)
- modify the Bezier curve tracker to query the underlying Bezier path to decide whether open- or closed-loop
- propagate API change (claosed-loop flag passed to ChBezierCurve, not to the lateral controller) to all path-following controllers
- fix the Bezier curve tracker to properly loop on a closed path

message:
Fixes to the CMake configuration for HMMWV_9BODY:

Remove the CMake options "HMMWV_9BODY_USE_IRRLICH" and "HMMWV_9BODY_USE_TERRAIN".  These are *not* configuration options, but rather execution options.  As such, they should be set elsewhere (right now, in the source file `demo_HMMWV_9body.cpp`)

The only configuration option is whether or not Irrlicht support is available for all chrono-T models.  Therefore, the configuration header template `HMMWV_9body_config.in` will only set a #define macro named `IRRLICHT_ENABLED` (with a value 0 or 1).

If Irrlicht support is available, then we include additional headers and optionally #define USE_IRRLICHT.

author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Fix bug related to variable offsets for timesteppers.

- First, note that this information (offsets in system-level arrays) is duplicated in chrono:  once in ChPhysicsItem and second in LCP variable objects.
- These offsets must be available on entry in the Advance() function of a given timestepper (e.g. for evaluating the system-level force vector)
- Offsets are read from both places (physics items and variables); an example of the latter is when applying forces on the two connected bodies from a spring-damper force element.  Note that offsets stored on the physics item can not be used for this purpose (this is because a ChLinkMarkers has handles to two body frames, not to the two bodies)
- The problem is that the offsets stored in the variables objects are updated through the system descriptor and that was not done until later on.
- The solution was to set up the system descriptor (inject variables and constraints) earlier on, in ChSystem::Integrate_Y_timestepper, before the call to Advance() and then update the offsets for all variables and constraints.
- The call to LCPprepare_inject() in ChSystem::StateSolveCorrection is not needed anymore and was removed

set up, the code is expected to deal with fine meshes better, since CUB is really fast. It remains
to see if this is the case.

GPU solver uses a lot less memory now, I moved the preprocessing stage to the iteration kernel by creating a new device function. Even though data is re-computer many times, it actually runs faster because there are fewer global memory accesses, (less data is saved and read from global). 
Because the data is not preprocessed, the memory used to store the data is not necessary, this saves a of GPU memory. Theoretically with a C1060 (4GB) it should be possible to run a simulation with 4 million particles and 22 million maximum contacts. I'm going to test this soon.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add function to return the terrain coefficient of friction for potential use in a tire model.

- This coefficient of friction value may be used by certain tire models to modify the tire characteristics, but it will have no effect on the interaction of the terrain with other objects (including tire models that do not explicitly use it).
- A concrete terrain class must implement the pure virtual function GetCoefficientFriction to return a coefficient of friction based on a specified (x,y) location.
- A concrete terrain model can make use of a user-provided functor object that returns a location-dependent friction value (derived from ChTerrain::FrictionFunctor).
- If no such functor object is provided, a concrete terrain model will return a constant value appropriate for that particular terrain model.

message:
Bugfix. The ChSystem::GetStiffnessMatrix() and ChSystem:::GetDampingMatrix()  functions returned K and R matrices that had the M mass matrix superimposed if there are atomic masses. This bug propagated to  ChSystem::DumpSystemMatrices(), ex. used by the Irrlicht GUIwhen pressing the F6 key ( "dump current matrices" ).  It did not affect the continuous dumping (F7 key) of the total system matrix, and it did not affect the system solution / time integration / etc., and it was not detectable in case you sed no atomic masses (ex. in FEA if you just used finite elements and masses came from elements only). So it was mostly confined to this "matrix dumping" diagnostic stuff.
Now fixed.

author: Alessandro Tasora <tasora@ied.unipr.it>
message:
New feature. When adding a convex hull collision shape, the invisible convex hull for the collision is automatically 'shrunk' by the inward margin, so that the convex hull algorithm can work with an outward margin of 'sphere swept' type. This is much more robust.
Note: if the inward safe margin is larger than the smaller approximate 'chord' of the hull, the inward margin is forced to be 0.2 times the chord.
Note: with large safe margins, the artifact is that the sharp corners behave smoothed from the collision point of view, i.e. all corners behave like they have a round fillet of radius = inward margin = shrinking offset.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Fix bugs in ChLoad:

1.
ChLoad<>::LoadIntLoadResidual_F() did not take into consideration loadable variables that may be inactive (e.g. because a node of an FEA is set fixed).
Same issue in ChLoadCustom::LoadIntLoadResidual_F().
The fix is based on a new virtual method (IsSubBlockActive) which must return a boolean indicating whether or not the specified sub-block of DOFs of a loadable element is active or not.

2.
The same mechanism, based on IsSubBlockActive, was implemented in ChLoadCustomMultiple::LoadIntLoadResidual_F().
The previous method, based on testing whether or not an object of type ChVariable was active or not was incorrect.  Indeed, a loadable can have more than one ChVariable objects per sub-block!

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Add new collision shape: cylindrical shell.

This collision shape represents a sphere-swept cylindrical shell, defined by a radius and halh-length of the skeleton cylinder and a radius of the sweeping sphere.
A cylshell is always aligned with the Y axis.

This collision type defaults to acting like a collision cylinder with inflated radius and half-length in the Bullet collision system and like a rounded cylinder in the Chrono::Parallel collision system.

The main purpose of this collision shape is to allow custom algorithms for certain collision pairs involving a cylshell.  In particular, the cylshell-box collision will be customized both in Bullet and Chrono::Parallel.

message: New classes:  ChModalSolveUndamped and ChModalSolveDamped . These act as managers of wrapped solvers of ChGeneralizedEigenvalueSolver or ChQuadraticEigenvalueSolver, respectively, and can manage multiple runs of such wrapped solvers in order to find eigenvalues clustered about some user-prescribed frequencies. author: Radu Serban <serban@engr.wisc.edu>
message:
Add support in unit_VEHICLE for a complete vehicle-powertrain-tires assembly.

These classes can can be used to create a (wheeled) vehicle + powertrain + tires assembly from given Chrono::Vehicle JSON specification files.  Such a vehicle always uses rigid tires (with contact geometry specified through a user-provided callback object of type ChTireContactCallback).  Optionally, contact geometry can be associated with the chassis body (through a user-specified callback of type ChChassisContactCallback).  Driver inputs are specified through a user-provided callback object of type ChDriverInputsCallback.

These classes can also be used with unit_PARALLEL, in which case the vehicle assembly must be constructed within a ChSystemParallel and the user-provided callback functions must also change the collision models for the wheel and chassis bodies to appropriate models, consistent with ChSystemParallel.

author: Radu Serban <serban@wisc.edu>
message:
Refactor ChVehicle (wheeled and tracked) to automatically manage synchronization and state advance for the associated powertrain.

- maintain vehicle-powertrain association through back pointers
- initialization of the powertrain system is intermediated by the vehicle (see ChWheeledVehicle::InitializePowertrain and ChTrackedVehicle::InitializePowertrain)
- after associating a powertrain system with a vehicle system, user code need not preserve the shared pointer to the powertrain system
- on Synchronize, the vehicle obtains the torque from the powertrain and the powertrain obtains the driveshaft speed from the associated driveline
- on Advance, the vehicle also advances the state of the associated powertrain

message:
Add the python binary directory to `which`'s PATH

Appends the directory of the executing Python bin to the path of the
search for `which` function. This should help with a corner case
on clusters which don't export the PATH variable correctly on nodes
of the executing environment since the absolute Python binary's path
ensures proper imports.

Also cleaned up some unused imports and `__all__` statements.

author: Logan Ward <ward.logan.t@gmail.com>
message:
Allow NWChem to restart single-point computations

As written, the NWCHarness does not write the geometry to the input
file for restart calculations. This is great for Driver computations
because it prevents the computation from restarting from the initial
geometry. However, the geometry is required for single point calculations
(esp Hessian, Gradient) because we use the geometry to determine
how NWChem rotates the coordinate system so that we can adjust
any direction-dependant quantities back to the initial coordinate system.

This change is simple: I add a flag that is set by the "driver" computation
to tell the NWCHarness not to write the geometry for restarts.
For clarity, the NWCOptimizerHarness calls the NWChemHardness
to make input files

message:
Get the scratch directory configuration before getting version

NWChem is an MPI parallel application, so it may not actually run
on the same node as that which is running QCEngine (this is the
case for Cray XC40s, which have MOM nodes from which you call
aprun to launch on compute nodes). Accordingly, we must apply some of
the job configuration information (e.g., scratch location) before
re-running.

author: Logan Ward <ward.logan.t@gmail.com>
message:
Added Hessian support and improved gradient accuracy

NWChem only prints gradients to an accuracy of 6 decimal places to
stdout. The full-accuracy versions are stored in checkpoint file of
NWChem. To access the full-precision gradients, we access and print them
using a Python script that runs during the NWChem execution.

See discussion here:
http://www.nwchem-sw.org/index.php/Special:AWCforum/st/id2155

I also implemented Hessian support while I was at it

author: Logan Ward <WardLT@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Allow NWChem to restart single-point computations (#333)

* Allow NWChem to restart single-point computations

As written, the NWCHarness does not write the geometry to the input
file for restart calculations. This is great for Driver computations
because it prevents the computation from restarting from the initial
geometry. However, the geometry is required for single point calculations
(esp Hessian, Gradient) because we use the geometry to determine
how NWChem rotates the coordinate system so that we can adjust
any direction-dependant quantities back to the initial coordinate system.

This change is simple: I add a flag that is set by the "driver" computation
to tell the NWCHarness not to write the geometry for restarts.
For clarity, the NWCOptimizerHarness calls the NWChemHardness
to make input files

author: Logan Ward <ward.logan.t@gmail.com>
message:
Allow NWChem to restart single-point computations

As written, the NWCHarness does not write the geometry to the input
file for restart calculations. This is great for Driver computations
because it prevents the computation from restarting from the initial
geometry. However, the geometry is required for single point calculations
(esp Hessian, Gradient) because we use the geometry to determine
how NWChem rotates the coordinate system so that we can adjust
any direction-dependant quantities back to the initial coordinate system.

This change is simple: I add a flag that is set by the "driver" computation
to tell the NWCHarness not to write the geometry for restarts.
For clarity, the NWCOptimizerHarness calls the NWChemHardness
to make input files

author: Levi Naden <levi.naden@choderalab.org>
message:
Enable Azure CI with custom images for proprietary code

This PR creates an Azure Pipeline which uses a custom Docker image we (MolSSI)
maintain and have exclusive access to through Azure Container Registry.

On this image we can house non-public code which will enable us to test
Engine through integrated CI on these codes securely.

I will say, there are lots of shennanigans and chain of aobut 20-25 different
commits of trying different things which got squished into this, but I can
confirm it works. Once this is merged in, I will activate it on the
Azure side for Engine itself and we can see it in action.

Right now, the image only contains a static MOPAC binary, but we could expand it
to include packages, or make other images and set up a strategy of different
containers to run through the pipeline. Thanks to Jonathan Moussa (godotalgorithm)
for helping get the binary.

message:
Implement the QCElemental Models into QCEngine

This is an overhaul to the QCEngine program to work with the
Pydantic Models which have been/will be added to the QCElemental package.

Right now, the models are all internal and will always return the
flattened dictionary of near-pure Python objects (numpy arrays being an exception).
The emitted objects should have no Pydantic in them, and right now will not
correctly emit in many casses; errors, procedures; if you try. As we continue
the integration of the QCElemental objects into QCA as a whole, we can
revisit this and get it working correctly.

This will need review since it changes a very large swath of code, all of which
had to be changed to get the tests passing.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: Support for faster C-based matrix and shape surface computation

Stats (Profiling 5 testcases):
  GLCM 9653 ms -> 7 ms
  GLDM 348 ms -> 7 ms
  NGTDM 133 ms -> 4ms

This commit adds two C Python extensions and associated tests:

* _cmatrices: C implementation for matrix computation associayed
  with GLCM, GLDM, GLDZM, GLRLM, GLSZM. and NGTDM features

* _cshape: C implementation for Shape surface computation

* tests/test_cmatrices: testing for matrix equality: Tests
  whether the python generated matrix is equal to the matrix
  generated by the C implementations (allows for machine precision errors)

Details
-------

* Add docstring to C modules

* Use of C implementation optional. At initialization, the package
  tries to use C, but if loading has failed, or calculation is forced
  to python, python is used. Note that the import of _cmatrices is done
  after initialization of logger. This ensures error will be logged
  if import fails.

* GLDM, NGTDM: C implementation accepts only one
  direction set of angles (i.e. 13 angles in a 3D image,
  4 angles in a 2D).

* GLSZM: Use "char" datatype for mask. (It is signed char
  in GLSZM).

* C code is consistent with C89 convention. All variables (pointers
  for python objects) are initialized at top of each block.

Optimizations
-------------

* GLSZM:

  - Uses "while" loops. This allows to reduce the memory usage.
    We observed that with recursive functions it was 'unexpectedly'
    failing.

  - Optimized search that finds a new index to process in
    the region growing.

Co-authored-by: Jean-Christophe Fillion-Robin <jchris.fillionr@kitware.com>

author: Joost van Griethuysen <joostjm@gmail.com>
message:
BUG: Fix bugs with empty angles in GLRLM and GLCM

In segment based mode, empty angles are removed from the calculation, but when calculating multiple voxel kernels, empty angles may presist (empty in some kernels, not in others). Exclude those angles from the calculations per voxel by setting them to NaN and using `nanmean` for combining angle results.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: Improve integrated resampling and cropping

Ensure that the resamplegrid of the cropped volume is aligned with the resampledgrid of the the original volume.
This is achieved by calculating the indices of the lower and upper bounds of the bounding box in terms of the resampled coordinate system.
The index for the lowerbound is rounded down and for the upper bound is rounded up to prevent data loss.
Additionally add padding for extra safty against data loss (mostly necessary when upsampling).
The index for the lowerbound is then brought back into the original Index space as a continuous index and is added to the continuous index of the new origin, this ensures that the resampling grid is aligned. This alignment is necessary to ensure that the outcome of the resampling is not influenced by the location of the bounding box.

Rename `cropTumorMaskToCube` to  `croptToTumorMask` to address any confusion caused by use of `cube`

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: compute shape features on labelMask

For the calculation of shape features the value of gray levels are unimportant, and the shape of the delineation is also captured in the labelmap.
By using the labelmap instead of the original image, it is not necessary to set voxels outside the delineation to a padding value, as these are by definition already 0 in the labelmap (not segmented).

Furthermore, only in shape calculation are voxels outside delineation excluded based upon their intensity value, in other feature classes these voxels are excluded based upon whether or not their indices are a part of `self.matrixCoordinates` (which is based upon the labelmap).
Therefore, by this change, there is no need to set the voxels outside the delineation to a paddingvalue during preprocessing.

 N.B. voxels still need to be set to a paddingvalue in `rlrl.py`, but this is already handled separatly by the code in `rlgl.py`, and is based upon labelmap.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: Allow a 0 value for output spacing when resampling

When resampling, allow the output spacing for any dimension to be set to 0 (the parameter 'resampledPixelSpacing' still needs to be a sequence of 3 elements, but the value of any element can be 0). Doing so will enable 'preserving' the original spacing, as 0 values are replaced with the original spacing for that dimension (original spacing of the mask). This way, it is possible to only resample in-plane (by setting the out-of-plane output spacing to 0).

Additionally, move the check between original and resampled spacing to after the size check (no resampling over dimensions for which bounding box size = 1) and build in a tolerance (1e-5 + 1e-8 * abs(resampledspacing)).

Finally, fix data type for resampled spacing in the validation schema for parameter files (change from integer to float).

author: Joost van Griethuysen <joostjm@gmail.com>
message:
BUG: Ensure consistency between numpy.histogram and numpy.digitize

Related to #219. Ensure numpy.histogram and numpy.digitize yield comparable results. The difference is caused by the fact that numpy.histogram treats the rightmost bin as a closed interval (i.e. values equal to the rightmost edge are included in the last bin). On the other hand, numpy.digitize treats all bins as half open (including the rightmost). In this latter case, values equal to the rightmost bin edge are given value `len(bins) + 1`.

Ensure consistent behaviour (with half open bins for all bins) by adding an extra bin edge when using fixed bin width (i.e. the rightmost edge is > max(targetValues)).
When using a fixed bin count, correct behaviour was already ensured by adding +1 to the last bin (which is guaranteed to be equal to max(targetValues). In this case, the +1 ensures nummpy.digitize considers these maximum values as part of the last bin, seeing as the edges are arranged such, that a specific number of bins is obtained).

On relation to #219: In that PR, the +1 to the rightmost bin was removed to allow 'switching off' binning by specifying bin-width 1. However, this changed did return the inconsistency between numpy.histogram and numpy.digitize, which is now corrected by this commit (by ensuring numpy.histogram is consistent with numpy.digitize, instead of the other way around).

message:

In commit 43578f7, use of class instance scope settings was changed to local scope settings allow correct parallel extraction using a shared instance of the extractor.
However, this also meant that the settings had to be passed to the function that loads the image and mask. While this was done so for the call to this function from inside RadiomicsFeatureExtractor, this was not done so for the call to this function in TestUtils, which is the workflow for loading the image/mask during testing. ENH: Enhance C GLSZM

Enhance C extension algorithm for calculating GLSZM. Instead of searching over entire image for voxels to process when growing a region, instantiate a stack (max size equal to number of voxels) to hold indices for voxels that have to be processed for the current region.

When an unprocessed voxel, belonging to the ROI is found, a region is started by pushing the index of that voxels to the stack. Then a loop is started where the last added voxel in the stack is popped and its neighbours are checked. If unprocessed and belonging to the same region (same gray level), indices for those voxels are also pushed to the stack. The loop then runs until stack is exhausted (i.e. no new neighbours available, indicating the region is complete). The number of loops are counted and are equal to the size of the zone.

Reset data type for mask from signed char back to char, as negative values are not needed anymore.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: Simplify computation of various GLCM features

Inverse Difference, Inverse Difference Moment, Inverse Difference Normalized, Inverse Difference Moment Normalized and Inverse Variance all use a |i=j| element, which is equal to the k_diff. This enables the use of p_x-y (`pxSuby`) and k_diff (`kValuesDiff`), which are precomputed in `_calculateCoefficients`. Note that for Inverse Variance, the first element (k = 0) is skipped, in accordance with the constraint of i not equal to j in the formula.

As `pxSuby` contains fewer elements and dimensions than `P_glcm`, replacing `P_glcm` by `pxSuby` and `numpy.abs(i-j)` by `kValuesDiff` simplifies the function, and less computations are required.

Update the feature formulas in the documentation accordingly.

The final calculated result should be identical (within machine precision), therefore the baseline does not need to be updated.

author: Jean-Christophe Fillion-Robin <jchris.fillionr@kitware.com>
message:
setup: use scikit-build to building of cmatrices and cshape extensions

This commit introduces a new dependencies to "scikit-built" and "cmake".

scikit-build is a drop-in replacement to setuptools.setup function
allowing to easily compile and package extensions (C/C++/Cython) by
bridging CMake and setuptools. See http://scikit-build.org

CMake is is an open-source, cross-platform family of tools designed
to build, test and package software. See https://cmake.org

Currently, scikit-build and cmake have to be explicitly (see [1]) installed
on the system. This could be done by simply doing:

  pip install scikit-build cmake

How does it work ?
------------------

In addition to simplifying setup.py, two new file have been added:

<root>
  |
  |---- CMakeLists.txt                          (1)
  .
  .
  .
  |--- src
  |     |--- CMakeLists.txt                     (2)
  .
  .

The first CMakeLists.txt specifies requirements for

* Python interpreter,

* the associated python libraries

* and a "PythonExtension" modules containing convenience CMake
  functions allowing to easily build extension by encapsulating
  system introspection and platform specific logic.

and include the subdirectory associated with the other CMakeLists.txt.

The second CMakeLists.txt is specific to "cmatrices" and "cshape"
extensions and it specifies:

* requirement for NumPy

Then, it declares:

* libraries for each extension, associate python extension specific properties

* and finally add an install rule specifying where in the package
  hierarchy the extension should be installed.

Et voila,

[1] Note that improvement to python packaging will be available shortly and
it will be possible to include scikit-build and cmake directly in pyproject.toml
See here for more details: https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0518/

author: Joost van Griethuysen <joostjm@gmail.com>
message:
ENH: Refactor command line and feature extractor

Commandline
- Instantiate feature extractor in main loop and pass it to the worker processes (this will only load the parameter file once, including all checks etc.)
- Simplify construction of `caseGenerator` (only contains case index and case, setting(overrides) are no longer needed as these are used to instantiate the extractor)
- Remove function '_buildGenerator', as construction of the generator is now a one-line code. Deprecated commandline switch `label` is now handled inside the `_parseOverrides` function, which in turn is called in `_processCases`.

FeatureExtractor
- RENAME CLASS FROM `RadiomicsFeaturesExtractor` TO `RadiomicsFeatureExtractor`, which shows better correspondence to the module name.
- Ensure that the feature extractor instance can be sent over a Pipe using pickle:
  - logger object is now defined as a global variable, not a variable of the extractor instance. This is done because this object often contains stream objects, which cannot be pickled
  - define geometryTolerance as a global variable, as this will then be set separately for each worker thread, as necessary. This prevents the tolerance from being set once in the parent process, but not in the child-processes.
  - Reduce the number of instance variables in the extractor as much as possible. Current variables retained (and pickled) are `settings`, `enabledImagetypes` `enabledFeatures`, `featureClassNames`
- Move parsing of shape-calculation settings to the function `computeShape()`
- Update docstring of `enableImageTypesByName` to reflect additions to PyRadiomics' filters
- Move the binCount warning to the instantiation of the extractor, resulting in 1 warning overall, instead of 1 warning for each extraction case.

Apply changes to rest of PyRadiomics' code to reflect changes made in feature extractor API.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ENH: Decrease computation time for GLCM

This is achieved by changing the iteration.
In the old version, iteration was done over all voxels in the segmentation, checking the entire neighbourhood of each voxel.
In this commit, iteration is now done over gray level twice (once as gray level i, once as j, corresponding to "center voxel" and "neighbour voxel").
Taking the intersection of indices to voxels that are neighbours to voxels with level i on the one hand and indices to voxels with gray level j on the other yields the indices to voxels that are BOTH have gray level j and are a neighbour to a voxel with gray level i.

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
BUG: fix filtering of diagonals in `rlgl.calculateRLGL`

For each angle, the found diagonals are filtered, where the goal is to filter out diagonals containing only the `padVal`.
However, currently, also diagonals containing one and only one voxel with a non-padVal value are excluded.
(in this case, the size of the array returned by numpy.nonzero is 1).

Change  `numpy.nonzero(x != padValue)[0].size > 1` to  `numpy.nonzero(x != padValue)[0].size > 0`,
so the filter also includes the diagonals where there is one voxel with a non-padVal value and
only excludes diagonals containing only padVal values.

ENH: Enable forced 2D texture extraction.

Add additional parameters to optionally force texture calculation to 2D. This is enabled by setting parameter `force2Dextraction` to True. Then, all angles moving across 'slices' are removed. For example, if enabled and dimension is 0, texture is extracted only in the xy-plane (with dimension 0 specifying the 'z' dimension as slice-dimension). Additionally, enable specifying custom distances between center voxel and neighbors. These distances are specified in the `distances` parameter as a list of integers. By default `disances = [1]`.

PEP 517 [1] provides a new standard format for specifying build-time
dependencies for Python packages. This format supercedes previous

author: Joost van Griethuysen <j.v.griethuysen@nki.nl>
message:
ADD: Add voxel-based extraction

Add a voxel based extraction, which outputs a dictionary of SimpleITK images instead of float values. Each voxel in the returned image represent the respective feature value for that region.

The local region can be defined as 'masked' or 'unmasked'. In unmasked mode, the region is defined as a cube with radius `kernelRadius` around the voxel: the kernel. If part of the kernel is outside of the image bounds, those parts are excluded.
In masked mode, the kernel is defined similar to unmasked mode, with additional exclusion of voxels that are outside the masked area (ROI).

This change also slightly changes the moment of several instantiation. In previous version, the the texture matrices in glcm, glrlm, etc. were calculated during initialization of the class. However, because for the voxel-based extraction they have to be calculated separately for each voxel, this functionality has been moved to the top of the `_calculateFeatures` (which runs when the features are acutally calculated).

N.B. This changes the API to the abstract feature class.
Features are now extracted by a call to `execute` instead of `calculateFeatures`. In addition to a name change, `execute` also directly returns the result (similar to usage of the feature extractor class). As before, calculated results remain available in the class under the `featureValues` attribute.

Adds a new section to the parameter file to allow customization of voxel-based extraction specific settings.

BUG: Force dType of discretized image array to int.

If input image array has a dType with max-value smaller than the number of bins, an overflow can occur, causing invalid values and subsequent faillure of texture matrix calculation (e.g. values of '0' or negative values can be present, causing index errors).
